short.en: the person in court who decides whether someone is guilty

def.en: The judge listened to both sides.

short.en: a person who hurts other people with violence

def.en: The police arrested the thugs who had been fighting outside the disco.

short.en: a person who is no longer alive

def.en: The police found a dead person in the forest.

short.en: something that is not right and not fair

def.en: He did him a great injustice.

short.en: not on purpose, through a mistake

def.en: I accidentally pressed the wrong key.

short.en: to say as a judge that someone is guilty and to give a punishment

def.en: The court sentenced the man to two years in prison.

short.en: when you ask people loudly to do something, for example through a loudspeaker

def.en: The police appeal to witnesses could be heard on the radio.

short.en: the door through which you leave a building

def.en: The exit that you should use in an emergency is on the right.

short.en: a small place in the countryside with few houses

def.en: We live in a small village in the mountains.

short.en: a small mountain

def.en: From the hill you can see the whole city.

short.en: the man at the head of a country who has this position through his family

def.en: The king lives in a large castle.

short.en: a tall tower by the sea with a light for the ships

def.en: The lighthouse shines all night so that the ships find their way.

short.en: not at the edge but in the centre

def.en: The hotel is in the middle of the old town.

short.en: a place that is so beautiful that it seems perfect

def.en: This beach is a paradise not only for children but also for adults.

short.en: many people who stand one behind the other and wait

def.en: A long queue stood in front of the museum.

short.en: when the sun disappears in the evening

def.en: We stayed by the sea until the sunset was over.

short.en: a bright point in the sky at night

def.en: Tonight you can see many stars.

short.en: so beautiful that it is like a dream

def.en: We had a dreamlike week by the sea.

short.en: a very tall, narrow building

def.en: From the tower you have a great view.

short.en: to no longer find the way because you went in the wrong direction

def.en: We got lost in the dark forest.

short.en: to walk on past a place or a person without stopping

def.en: He walked past the café without seeing us.

short.en: to walk again after standing or after a break, not to stay standing

def.en: Please do not stop, but walk on!

q.en: <g>Could you</g> please be a bit quieter? It's already after 10 p.m.

a.en: Sorry, I <g>didn't know</g> that. I'll be quieter right away.

q.en: Where <g>may</g> I leave my stroller?

a.en: Best in the basement; unfortunately you <g>can't</g> leave it in the stairwell.

q.en: Why does it smell so good here in the stairwell?

a.en: Mrs Kowalski always bakes a cake for the whole neighbourhood on Sundays.

q.en: Since when have you been living in this building?

a.en: We have been living here for five years already, and we like it very much.

q.en: Shall we buy <g>both</g> milk <g>and</g> eggs at the market?

a.en: Sure, both are fresher there than at the supermarket.

q.en: The trousers <g>that</g> I bought last week are unfortunately broken.

a.en: I'm sorry! <g>Have</g> you already <g>looked</g> for the receipt?

q.en: Why are you writing a complaint?

a.en: <g>Because</g> the package arrived damaged and I want my money back.

q.en: Can you help me for a moment <g>to fill in</g> the exchange form?

a.en: Sure, I'll gladly do that for you.

q.en: He <g>should</g> already be home now, right?

a.en: Yes, he's probably already sitting in front of the TV.

q.en: <g>Whose</g> account is that, actually?

a.en: That's <g>my daughter's</g> account, I just manage it.

q.en: Why did you cancel the insurance <g>although</g> it was so cheap?

a.en: <g>Because</g> the service was unfortunately very bad.

q.en: <g>Have</g> you already <g>called</g> the consumer advice centre?

a.en: No, not yet, but I <g>will do</g> it tomorrow.

q.en: How has your diet changed <g>since</g> you have been living in Germany?

a.en: We eat much more vegetables now than before.

q.en: Do you prefer eating regularly at home, or do you often eat on the go?

a.en: I actually always cook myself, it's healthier and cheaper.

q.en: Why <g>did</g> you <g>wait</g> so long for the recipe?

a.en: I waited <g>until</g> I had all the ingredients in the fridge.

q.en: What <g>were</g> the results of the survey on eating habits?

a.en: Most people eat less meat today than before.

q.en: What <g>were</g> you most annoyed <g>about</g> in the language course?

a.en: <g>About</g> how complicated the grammar is.

q.en: <g>Who</g> do you actually speak your native language <g>with</g>?

a.en: Only with my family, otherwise I speak German.

q.en: Have you been here long, or have you only lived in Germany for a short time?

a.en: I've already been living here for three years.

q.en: What <g>surprised</g> you most when you <g>came</g> here?

a.en: <g>That</g> the shops are closed on Sundays.

q.en: Will the patient be operated on tomorrow?

a.en: Yes, the operation <g>will take place</g> at nine o'clock.

q.en: Why <g>did</g> you <g>go</g> to the emergency room?

a.en: While doing sports, I <g>not only</g> hurt my knee <g>but also</g> my arm.

q.en: What do you need this form <g>for</g>?

a.en: I need it <g>in order to</g> register at the clinic.

q.en: How long does the examination take approximately?

a.en: It usually doesn't take longer than half an hour.

q.en: <g>Is</g> the rubbish actually <g>sorted</g> properly here?

a.en: Yes, the waste <g>is</g> <g>sorted</g> into three different bins.

q.en: <g>Have</g> you already <g>saved</g> energy this year?

a.en: Yes, we <g>have</g> <g>replaced</g> our old lamps with LED lamps.

q.en: Why do you only buy seasonal vegetables now?

a.en: <g>Because</g> it's better for the environment and usually cheaper too.

q.en: What else can we do for the climate?

a.en: We could use the bicycle instead of the car more often.

q.en: What are you looking forward <g>to</g> most at the festival?

a.en: The evening concerts — the bands are really great.

q.en: What is the new exhibition at the museum actually about?

a.en: About modern art from the last ten years.

q.en: <g>So</g>, how was the library tour?

a.en: Really interesting, we <g>learned</g> a lot about old books.

q.en: <g>Can</g> you recommend a good street festival to me?

a.en: Sure, the summer festival in the old town is great every year.

q.en: I'm calling about the job advertisement. <g>Could you</g> tell me if the position is still available?

a.en: Yes, the position is still available. Would you like to apply?

q.en: <g>I would like</g> more information about the working hours.

a.en: No problem, here we usually work from eight to five.

q.en: What would you do <g>if</g> you <g>didn't get</g> the job?

a.en: Then I <g>would</g> simply <g>apply</g> to another company.

q.en: How was your job interview today?

a.en: Pretty good, I think they've decided to hire me.

q.en: Should we go running <g>before</g> it gets too hot?

a.en: Good idea, then let's start at seven o'clock.

q.en: Who had the <g>fastest</g> run in the competition?

a.en: That <g>was</g> Lukas, he's really in top form.

q.en: Are you taking part in the charity run on Saturday?

a.en: Sure, <g>I've</g> already <g>picked up</g> my start number.

q.en: Why do you actually train every day?

a.en: <g>Because</g> I simply feel much better afterwards.

q.en: Who's cooking today <g>while</g> I bathe the baby?

a.en: I <g>can</g> take care of that, no problem.

q.en: Do I <g>have to</g> apply for the daycare place already now?

a.en: You <g>don't need to</g> do that right away, but don't wait too long.

q.en: How are you doing as new parents?

a.en: Exhausting, but we're really happy.

q.en: Who's picking up the kids from school today?

a.en: <g>Any of us</g> can do it, we don't have a fixed rule for that.

q.en: <g>After</g> I had passed the exam, I found a job right away.

a.en: I'm really happy for you!

q.en: <g>Had</g> you <g>worked</g> in Germany before the interview?

a.en: No, but I <g>had already gained</g> a lot of experience in my home country before.

q.en: How's the recognition of your diploma going?

a.en: Pretty well, I'm just waiting for the last documents now.

q.en: What do you think of your new colleagues?

a.en: Very nice, they really <g>helped</g> me on the first day.

q.en: The car <g>has to be repaired</g> by a volunteer before we can leave.

a.en: No problem, Mr Meyer is already taking care of it.

q.en: <g>Because of the</g> bad weather, the trip won't take place tomorrow.

a.en: Too bad, then let's just postpone it to next week.

q.en: Are you also involved in volunteering for the neighbourhood help?

a.en: Yes, I've been helping there regularly for a year.

q.en: What motivated you to get involved as a volunteer?

a.en: I just <g>wanted</g> to give something back to the community.

q.en: Is that the flat <g>for which</g> you applied?

a.en: Exactly that one, I really hope I get it.

q.en: Do you know a place <g>where</g> you can live cheaply?

a.en: Yes, there are still some <g>affordable</g> flats on the outskirts.

q.en: How high are the utility costs in your new house?

a.en: Luckily not too high, <g>because</g> the house is well insulated.

q.en: When can you move into the new flat?

a.en: Already next week, we're really looking forward <g>to it</g>.

q.en: Is that the <g>completed</g> application for naturalisation?

a.en: Exactly, I <g>finished</g> everything this morning.

q.en: Do I need <g>either</g> my passport <g>or</g> my ID card for the appointment?

a.en: It's best if you <g>bring</g> both documents <g>with you</g>.

q.en: How long does the integration course take altogether?

a.en: For me it <g>took</g> about eight months.

q.en: Do you feel at home in Germany by now?

a.en: Yes, I think <g>I've</g> really <g>arrived</g>.

q.en: Are we going away this year, <g>or</g> would we rather stay home?

a.en: I'd <g>most like to travel</g> somewhere again.

q.en: When are you coming <g>back</g> from your trip?

a.en: Next Sunday, I'm already looking forward <g>to</g> unpacking.

q.en: Have you ever been to the youth hostel in the old town?

a.en: Yes, last year, it <g>was</g> really cheap and cosy.

q.en: Have you heard about the burglary in the neighbourhood?

a.en: Yes, luckily the police <g>were able to</g> arrest the burglar quickly.

task.en:
Situation: You and your neighbour live in an apartment building. The basement and the stairwell have been messy for a long time.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to tidy it up.
These points will help you:
When? (date, time)
What first? (basement, stairwell)
Baby stroller – where to put it?
What to bring? (gloves, garbage bags)
Inform other neighbours? (note, notice)

q.en: Hi, Julia! It's great <g>that</g> we can plan this together. The basement and the stairwell really look chaotic – we should tidy them up.

a.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we do it on Saturday morning?
Does that work for you, Mark?

q1.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest we first tidy up the basement and then the stairwell.
What do you think?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the baby strollers in the basement.
We could find a fixed spot for them.
How do you find that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we bring gloves and garbage bags.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we write a note for the mailboxes so that everyone knows.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether everyone will actually read it.
Maybe it would be best if we also put up a notice in the stairwell.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just meet at the basement entrance at 10 o'clock.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I would suggest that we also tell the landlord about the broken lamp in the stairwell.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll do it like this: Saturday at 10 o'clock at the basement, we'll <g>bring</g> gloves and garbage bags <g>along</g>, and I'll write the note for the mailboxes. I'm already looking forward to it! See you Saturday!

task.en:
Situation: You and your neighbour want to organize a small party for the neighbourhood in the courtyard.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to organize it.
These points will help you:
When? (date, time)
Where exactly? (courtyard, garden)
Tables and chairs – where to put them?
What to bring? (food, drinks, music)
Cars – what about parking?

q.en: Hi, David! Shall we plan the party for our neighbourhood together? I think it'll be a nice chance <g>to get to know</g> the new neighbours.

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
How about we do it next Saturday afternoon?
What do you think, Julia?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest we put the tables in the courtyard — we have more space there than in the garden.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the playground.
We could let the children play at the playground while the tables stand in the courtyard.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that every family brings something to eat.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: I'll bring the speaker, and you take care of the drinks.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether there will be enough parking spots for the guests.
Maybe it would be best if we ask the neighbours to park their cars in the garage.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just hang a note in the hallway so everyone knows.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we meet in the courtyard in the morning to get everything ready.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll meet Saturday morning in the courtyard, put the tables there, the children will play at the playground, I'll bring the music and you the drinks. I'm already looking forward <g>to our party</g>! See you Saturday!

task.en:
Situation: You're going on vacation for ten days next week and want to organize neighbourhood help with your neighbour.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll organize it.
These points will help you:
When exactly? (dates from–to)
Watering the flowers – how often?
Picking up mail and packages?
Handing over the key – when and where?
Return favour – what can you do in return?

q.en: Hi, Mark! I <g>have</g> a favour to ask you: I'm going on vacation for ten days next week and wanted to plan with you how we can best organize it.

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that I could take care of your flowers every day.
Is that okay with you, Anna?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that you could get my mail from the mailbox.
Would that be okay for you?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the packages.
I could just pick up the packages too, if any arrive.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that I give you my spare key beforehand.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: just let me know exactly when you're leaving.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether I can just ask that of you.
Maybe it would be best if I did you a favour in return.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just borrow your tools for my shelf, that would already be enough.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that I bring you the key tomorrow.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, I'll water your flowers every day, pick up the mail and packages, and you'll bring me the key tomorrow and lend me your tools for the shelf. I'm already looking forward <g>to helping</g> you! See you tomorrow!

task.en:
Situation: You want to organize a house meeting with a neighbour so that all the tenants can live together better as a community.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll organize it.
These points will help you:
When and where? (date for the meeting)
Which topics? (noise, waste separation)
Who invites the tenants?
How do we agree in the end? (house rules)
Who takes care of what?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I think we should organize a house meeting <g>so that</g> we can live together better as a community. Do you feel like planning that with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we try to find a date that works for all the tenants.
What do you think, Nina?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we first think about which topics matter, for example how we can try to avoid arguments.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about waste separation.
We could try to set up shared rules for waste separation.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we manage to invite all the tenants in time.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: it would be important to be considerate of each other when we talk about noise.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll manage to satisfy everyone.
Maybe it would be best if we try to agree on shared house rules at the end.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just share the tasks: I'll take care of organizing the room, and you handle the invitations.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we try to write a short summary so everyone is informed.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll find a date that works for everyone, I'll organize the room, you'll invite the tenants, and in the end we'll agree together on house rules. I'm already looking forward <g>to the meeting</g>! See you then!

task.en:
Situation: You want to plan a small barbecue in the garden with a neighbour while respecting the house rules.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll organize it.
These points will help you:
When? (date, time, respect quiet hours)
Where to grill? (lawn, terrace)
Inform other tenants?
What to do if it rains? (common rooms)
Cleaning up and parking for guests?

q.en: Hi, Anna! I <g>wanted</g> to ask whether we could plan a little barbecue in the garden together. What do you think?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we do it on a Saturday, but we have to respect the quiet hours from 10 pm.
What do you think, David?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we grill on the terrace, because according to the house rules we're not allowed to grill on the lawn.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the neighbours who aren't joining.
We could write a note beforehand, because we're supposed to inform all the tenants about such parties according to the house rules.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that everyone who wants to brings something to eat.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we can use the common room if it rains.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether there'll be enough parking spots for the guests.
Maybe it would be best if we ask the guests not to park right in front of the house, because according to the house rules you're not allowed to park there.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just clean up together after the party and tidy the garden again, since we have to do that anyway according to the house rules.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we air out the room briefly at the end so that everything smells fresh again.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll grill on the terrace on Saturday, inform all the neighbours beforehand, everyone <g>brings</g> something <g>along</g>, and afterwards we'll clean up together. I'm already looking forward to our party! See you Saturday!

task.en:
Situation: Your neighbour is often inconsiderately loud, both in the evenings and on weekends. You want to plan a conversation with him together with another neighbour.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'd like to have the conversation.
These points will help you:
When will you talk to him?
What exactly will you say? (friendly, without accusations)
What compromise will you suggest?
What to do if he doesn't react?
How will you check in with each other afterwards?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I <g>wanted</g> to talk to you about how we can speak with our loud neighbour. The noise is really getting to be too much.

a.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I suggest that we talk to him together, because he's noisy both in the evenings and on weekends.
What do you think, Mark?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we stay friendly and tell him that we want neither to argue nor to ignore him, but to find a solution.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about when to talk to him.
We could ring the bell on Saturday morning, since he's usually home then.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we offer him a compromise, for example both fixed quiet hours and fewer parties during the week.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we shouldn't accuse him of being inconsiderate, but calmly explain how annoying the noise is for us.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether he'll even listen.
Maybe it would be best if we tell him that otherwise we'd have to file an official complaint.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just have the conversation together, so he feels less attacked.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we check in briefly afterwards about how the conversation went.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll ring the bell together on Saturday morning, talk calmly to him about the noise, suggest a compromise, and afterwards we'll check in with each other. I hope the conversation goes well! See you Saturday!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to go shopping together because you still need quite a few things for the week.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll go shopping.
These points will help you:
When and where to shop? (respect opening hours)
What's on the shopping list?
Where are there special offers?
Check supplies at home – what's really missing?
How will you split the cost at the checkout?

q.en: Hi, Julia! Should we go shopping together? I think we still need quite a few things for the week.

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first check the supermarket's opening hours.
What do you think, Alex?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we write a shared shopping list beforehand so we don't forget anything.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also check what we already have at home.
We could check our supplies first before we go.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we go to the supermarket that currently has special offers.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we only buy fresh fruit and vegetables, no expensive brands.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll get everything in one place.
Maybe it would be best if we go to the cheap supermarket first and get the rest later.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just split the cost at the checkout.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we go tomorrow afternoon, before it gets too crowded.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll write the list first, check our supplies, go to the supermarket with the best deals tomorrow afternoon, and split the cost at the checkout. I'm already looking forward <g>to</g> shopping! See you tomorrow!

task.en:
Situation: You want to plan a joint online order with a friend to save on shipping costs.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll do it.
These points will help you:
What do you want to order?
Where will you find out about it beforehand? (reviews, prices)
By when do you need to decide? (offer)
How will you split the cost?
When will you meet to pick up the package?

q.en: Hi, Mark! I <g>wanted</g> to plan a joint order with you, that way we save on shipping costs. Are you up for it?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first figure out for ourselves what we really want to order.
What do you think, Julia?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we inform ourselves about the reviews beforehand.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the time.
We could hurry, since the offer ends this evening.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we decide on the cheaper brand.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: I'll place the order, and you transfer me your share later.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure when the package will arrive.
Maybe it would be best if we arrange a pickup time right now.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just meet on Friday afternoon to pick up the package together.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that I look forward to the new product already and send off the order right away.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll decide on the cheaper brand, I'll order it this evening, and we'll meet on Friday afternoon <g>to</g> pick up the package. I'm already looking forward to it! See you Friday!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend ordered something online together, but the product unfortunately arrived damaged.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll file the complaint.
These points will help you:
What is damaged or defective?
Who will write the complaint?
How will you send the product back?
What to do if the seller doesn't respond?
Replacement or refund?

q.en: Hi, David! <g>Have</g> you already <g>opened</g> the package? I think there's unfortunately a mistake – the product we <g>ordered</g> is damaged.

a.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I suggest that we write a complaint right away, because this isn't our fault, but rather a shipping error.
What do you think, Anna?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we contact the seller who sent us the order.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also take a photo.
We could take a photo of the product that is damaged, so we can send it as proof.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we don't just keep it, but rather send it straight back.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we ask for a replacement that gets sent to us quickly.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the seller will react quickly.
Maybe it would be best if we set a deadline that is clear, so they know by when they have to respond.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just ask for our money back if no replacement comes that works for us.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we don't file the complaint verbally, but rather in writing, so we have everything documented.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll take a photo, write a formal complaint, <g>send</g> the damaged product <g>back</g>, and ask for a replacement. I hope it works out quickly! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You want to order a present online with a friend for a mutual friend.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll place the order.
These points will help you:
What will you put in the shopping cart?
Which payment method will you use?
Where should the delivery go? (shipping address)
How long is the delivery time?
Who will order it and note the order number?

q.en: Hi, Mark! I <g>wanted</g> to order a present for Anna with you. Do you have time to plan that with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first put something suitable in the shopping cart.
What do you think, Nina?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we pay attention to the shipping costs, so it doesn't get too expensive.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the delivery time.
We could check how long the delivery time is, since her birthday is already next week.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we use your apartment as the shipping address, so we can wrap it together.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: I'll pay by card, that's the fastest payment method.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll get the present in time.
Maybe it would be best if we note down the order number so we can track the delivery.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just keep the delivery note safe, in case we need to file a complaint.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we send off the order tonight.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll put the present in the shopping cart, I'll pay by card, the delivery will go to my address, and we'll note down the order number. I'm already looking forward to Anna's face! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You and your roommate received a shared invoice that you need to pay together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll pay the invoice.
These points will help you:
How much is the amount?
By when is the deadline?
Who will make the transfer?
How will you split the amount?
What can you do to avoid a dunning notice?

q.en: Hi, Julia! I got the invoice <g>that</g> we need to pay together. Do you want to quickly plan how we'll do that?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first check the amount that we have to pay.
What do you think, David?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we pay attention to the deadline that is on the invoice.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about who transfers the money.
We could use the account that we have together.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we just split the amount that we have to share.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: I'll make the transfer that we should send today.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll still make the deadline.
Maybe it would be best if we avoid the fee that we'd otherwise have to pay.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also check the contract that we signed once more.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we remind each other in case someone forgets the payment.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, I'll transfer the money today, we'll split the amount, and we'll check the contract together. That way we won't get a dunning notice! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: Your old washing machine is broken. You want to plan with your roommate how you'll buy a new one.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll go shopping.
These points will help you:
Where will you compare prices?
What quality do you need? (reviews)
Is there a discount or a reduced model?
Is the appliance really worth it?
What to do if you need to exchange it? (receipt)

q.en: Hi, Anna! Our old washing machine is broken. Should we plan together how we'll buy a new one?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first do a price comparison.
What do you think, Mark?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we also compare the quality and read a few reviews.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also watch out for discounts.
We could check if there's a discounted model right now.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we only buy an appliance that's really worth it.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we save for one more week, then we'll have enough money for a better model.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we should wait that long.
Maybe it would be best if we keep the receipt safe, in case we need to exchange it.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just go to the store together on the weekend and take a look at it in person.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we quickly compare the best offers online beforehand.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll compare prices online, read the reviews, and on the weekend we'll go to the store together. I hope we find a good deal! See you Saturday!

task.en:
Situation: You want to open a joint checking account at the bank with a friend.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll do it.
These points will help you:
When is the bank branch open?
What do you need to bring? (ID)
Who opens the account, who becomes co-holder?
How long might it take?
What will you do afterwards? (online banking, PIN)

q.en: Hi, Nina! Should we go to the bank together and open a joint account? I think that <g>would be</g> practical for us.

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we go tomorrow morning, the bank branch should open at nine.
What do you think, Alex?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we bring our ID cards, we'll probably need them.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the waiting time.
We could go early, it could otherwise take longer.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that I open the account and you become a co-holder.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: afterwards we set up online banking right away, that shouldn't take long.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll get the PIN right away.
Maybe it would be best if we ask, since it probably comes by mail normally.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also ask whether our old ID cards are still valid.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we check the account balance right afterwards, that could be helpful.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll go to the bank tomorrow morning, bring our ID cards, I'll become a co-holder, and afterwards we'll set up online banking. I'm already looking forward to it! See you tomorrow!

task.en:
Situation: You now need your own account too and want to compare different banks' offers with a friend.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll compare the offers.
These points will help you:
How much is the account fee?
Is insurance included?
What's the interest rate on the overdraft?
Savings book or credit card – which matters more?
When will you open the new account?

q.en: Hi, Anna! I need my own account now too. Can you help me <g>compare</g> the offers?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first compare the amount of the account fee.
What do you think, Julia?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we also look at the conditions of the insurance some banks offer.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the overdraft facility.
We could compare the interest on the overdraft, in case you're ever in the red.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we also look at the benefits of the savings book.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we also check whether a credit card is included in the price of the account.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure which bank fits best.
Maybe it would be best if we go through each bank's website together.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just summarize the results of our comparison at the end.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we open the best bank's account tomorrow.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll first compare the account fee, the interest, and the insurance, and tomorrow you'll open the account at the best bank. I'm happy to help you with it! See you tomorrow!

task.en:
Situation: You can't find your bank card and don't know whether you lost it or it was stolen. You want to plan with a friend what to do now.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll proceed.
These points will help you:
Block the card first – how?
Theft or lost?
File a police report?
Notify the bank
How do you get a replacement card?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I can't find my bank card anymore. Can you help me <g>think</g> about what to do now?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we call the emergency blocking hotline first, so no one can withdraw your money.
What do you think, David?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we think about whether the card was stolen or whether I just lost it.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the police.
We could file a police report, in case the card was stolen.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we notify the bank right afterwards.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we ask right away how long it takes for you to get a replacement card.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the bank can replace the card right away.
Maybe it would be best if we clarify that directly at the bank branch.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just go to the bank branch together, so you're not alone.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we call the emergency blocking hotline right now, before we go.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll call the emergency blocking hotline now, then go to the bank branch together, and you'll file a police report in case the card was stolen. I'm with you! See you in a bit!

task.en:
Situation: You and your roommate are considering whether to keep your home contents insurance or cancel another insurance policy.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll proceed.
These points will help you:
Do you really need the insurance? (voluntary or necessary)
What does the insurance coverage include?
How high is the deductible?
Should you cancel the old insurance?
When will you sort this out?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I've been <g>thinking</g> about our home contents insurance. Should we think together about whether we really need it?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we keep it, although it costs extra money, because it protects us in case of a break-in.
What do you think, Mark?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we check exactly what the insurance coverage includes, although that takes a bit of time.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the deductible.
We could check how high the deductible is, although that's often written small in the contract.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we keep the insurance, although it's voluntary, because it gives us peace of mind.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we cancel the old car insurance, although we've had it for a long time, because it's too expensive.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether cancelling is that simple.
Maybe it would be best if we find out more, although that might be a bit complicated.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just write the cancellation letter, although we don't have an answer from the new insurer yet.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we sort everything out today, although we don't really have time.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll keep the home contents insurance, cancel the old car insurance, and sort out everything important today. It's sensible, although it's a bit of work! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You're going on vacation soon and want to plan a consultation with the insurance agent with a friend.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare for the meeting.
These points will help you:
When will you schedule the consultation?
Do you need travel insurance?
How long is the notice period on the old contract?
Should you visit the consumer advice centre first?
Who will sign the new contract?

q.en: Hi, Julia! We're going on vacation soon. Should we schedule a consultation with the insurance agent?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we schedule the consultation for next week first.
What do you think, Anna?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we ask her about good travel insurance.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the old contract.
We could ask how long the notice period is for our old contract.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we get information from the consumer advice centre beforehand.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we also ask about the exact payment date, so we don't forget anything.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we should sign the contract right away.
Maybe it would be best if we discuss everything calmly at home first.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just prepare the letter of termination for the old contract already.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we also ask about a suitable savings plan before we sign the new contract.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll schedule the consultation, ask about the travel insurance and the notice period, and prepare the letter of termination. I'm already looking forward to the vacation! See you next week!

task.en:
Situation: Although you cancelled in time, a fee was still charged from your account. You want to plan with a friend how to sort this out.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll proceed.
These points will help you:
What proof do you need? (confirmation of the cancellation)
Will you write or call first?
How will you demand the money back?
What deadline will you set?
What to do if the company doesn't respond?

q.en: Hi, David! I just saw <g>that</g> a fee was still charged from my account, although I cancelled in time. Can you help me sort this out?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we look for the confirmation first, because we need it as proof.
What do you think, Nina?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we write to the company, because we have proof.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also call them.
We could call first, and then write an email as well.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we demand the transfer back, nevertheless we should stay friendly.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we write exactly that we cancelled in time.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether they'll pay the money back right away.
Maybe it would be best if we set a clear deadline.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also ask whether we can revoke the contract again if necessary.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we send the email today, but read it through again first.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll look for the confirmation, call them, write an email with the proof, and set a deadline for the refund. I'm happy to help you with it! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You want to have breakfast together with a friend this weekend and compare your eating habits.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll organize the breakfast.
These points will help you:
Sweet or salty – what will there be?
Is anyone vegetarian?
What if someone wants to eat low-calorie?
Who will go shopping? (vending machine or supermarket)
When will you meet?

q.en: Hi, Mark! Should we have breakfast together this weekend? I<g>'d like</g> to <g>compare</g> our eating habits sometime.

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we make both something sweet and something salty, so there's something for everyone.
What do you think, Alex?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we also think about vegetarian options, in case someone doesn't eat meat.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about low-calorie things.
We could bring some fruit instead of cake, that's lower in calories.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we meet as soon as we're really hungry, so around nine.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: I'll buy fresh bread, and you bring something from the vending machine, in case we're still missing something.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the vending machine will already have coffee at that time.
Maybe it would be best if we make fresh coffee instead.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just make enough so that we're all really full at the end.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we go shopping together tonight already.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll go shopping tonight, meet for breakfast tomorrow at nine, and I'll make sweet and salty things while you take care of the coffee. I'm already looking forward to it! See you tomorrow!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to plan a nostalgic cooking night and recreate old family recipes from your childhood.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll organize the cooking night.
These points will help you:
What did you often eat back then?
What did you like to eat and drink most as children?
Who will bring which dish?
Will you ask your parents for the recipes?
When and where will you meet?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I've <g>been thinking</g> about our childhood recently. Do you remember what you often used to eat at home? Should we plan a cooking night and recreate a few old dishes?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first think about what we often had back then, for example potato soup.
What do you think, Julia?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we also think about what we liked to eat most as kids.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the drinks.
We could think about what we always drank back then, maybe homemade juice.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that everyone brings a dish their mother often cooked back then.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: my grandma always baked an apple cake, I'll bring that.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we still remember all the recipes.
Maybe it would be best if we ask our parents beforehand how it was back then.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just ask how long the preparation took last time.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we do the whole thing like it was at the family parties back then – with lots of music and guests.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll recreate the old family recipes, I'll bring my grandma's apple cake, and we'll ask our parents for the recipes. I'm already looking forward to the cooking night! See you Saturday!

task.en:
Situation: You've gained weight recently and want to plan with a friend how to eat more healthily and move more.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll change your habits.
These points will help you:
What do you want to change? (diet, exercise)
How often will you meet regularly?
How will you track your progress?
What will you do when it's hard?
How will you support each other?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I've <g>gained</g> quite a bit of weight lately. Should we plan together how to eat more healthily?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we meet regularly, that's why I'd say every Wednesday.
What do you think, David?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we cook together, that's why we also save time.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about exercise.
We could go running three times a week, it's tiring, but still we'll definitely manage it together.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we write down our progress, that's why we'll keep a little journal.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we eat more mindfully, that's why we'll buy fewer ready meals.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll always keep it up.
Maybe it would be best if we allow ourselves a day off sometimes, but still stick with it.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just stay motivated, even if it's sometimes hard.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we support each other, that's why we'll write each other a short message every evening.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll meet every Wednesday, cook together, go running three times a week, and write to each other every evening. I'm already looking forward to our change! See you Wednesday!

task.en:
Situation: A mutual friend's birthday is coming up soon. You want to cook and bake together with a friend.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll organize it.
These points will help you:
Which family recipe will you use for the cake?
What's missing in the kitchen cabinet?
What portion size do you need?
How will you set the guest table?
What will you do with the leftovers afterwards?

q.en: Hi, Nina! Julia's birthday is coming up soon. Should we cook and bake together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we bake the birthday cake using my mother's recipe.
What do you think, Anna?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we first check the kitchen cabinet to see what ingredients we still have.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the number of guests.
We could calculate the portion size based on how many people are coming.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we also try a second family recipe, maybe your grandma has one too.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we set the guest table nicely, with flowers and candles.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll have enough time for everything.
Maybe it would be best if we start baking already the day before.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just give the leftovers to the neighbours afterwards, so nothing gets thrown away.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we taste everything together at the end, before the guests arrive.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll bake the cake using the family recipe, set the guest table nicely, and give the leftovers to the neighbours afterwards. I'm already looking forward to cooking! See you tomorrow!

task.en:
Situation: You want to plan a survey about eating habits with a friend and present the results later.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll conduct the survey.
These points will help you:
What questions will you ask in the survey?
Who will you survey?
How will you collect the answers?
How will you present the results? (statistics, average)
By when will the survey be finished?

q.en: Hi, David! I<g>'d like</g> to <g>do</g> a survey about our eating habits. Do you feel like planning that with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first find out the opinion of the majority, so we'll ask a lot of people.
What do you think, Mark?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we let the questions be answered by our class.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the evaluation.
We could collect the answers of the participants in a table.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we calculate the average of all the answers at the end.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we show the results of the survey as a small statistic.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll find enough participants.
Maybe it would be best if we also ask the colleagues of my sister.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just briefly summarize the trend of the answers at the end.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we finish the survey by the end of the week.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll ask our class the questions, collect the answers, and calculate the average for the statistic at the end. I'm already looking forward to the results! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You want to eat more healthily and prepare meals for the whole week with a friend.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare the food.
These points will help you:
What will you cook? (varied, balanced)
How big are the portions?
How many food storage containers do you need?
How will you make sure you get enough vitamins and fibre?
When will you meet to cook?

q.en: Hi, Anna! I want to eat healthier. Should we cook meals for the week together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we plan a varied menu, so it doesn't get boring.
What do you think, Alex?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we make sure to have a balanced mix of vegetables and protein.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the portions.
We could make the portions the same size, so it's fair for both of us.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we buy enough food storage containers before we start.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we make sure to get enough fibre, for example with brown rice.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we're getting all the important vitamins.
Maybe it would be best if we add some fruit as a snack.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also roughly calculate the calories per portion.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we meet to cook on Sunday afternoon already.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll cook a varied, balanced menu on Sunday, pack it into food storage containers, and take some fruit as a snack too. I'm already looking forward to cooking! See you Sunday!

task.en:
Situation: Your new colleague is from another country. You want to plan with a colleague how to help her settle in here.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll do it.
These points will help you:
What is probably the most unfamiliar for her?
Which local rules will you explain?
How will you show her the city?
What has surprised you yourself since you've been here?
When will you invite her?

q.en: Hi, Julia! Our new colleague is from another country. Should we plan together how we'll show her around here?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we explain the most important rules to her, because since I've been working here, I know how many misunderstandings there can be.
What do you think, Nina?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we tell her what surprised us ourselves since we've been living here.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about her habits.
We could ask what feels foreign to her since she's been here.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we show her around the city, so she feels familiar with it faster.
Do you agree with that?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we invite her to our place, since I started doing that, new colleagues have felt a lot more comfortable.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether she already feels comfortable asking us questions.
Maybe it would be best if we tell her ourselves what expectations we had at the start.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also explain how our culture has developed, that will surely interest a lot of people.
Does that work for you?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we invite her for lunch already next week.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll explain the most important rules to her, show her around the city, and invite her for lunch next week. I'm already looking forward <g>to getting to know</g> her better! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You want to organize an evening with a friend where everyone talks about their language biographies.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare the evening.
These points will help you:
What will the participants talk about first?
Who do they remember from their language learning?
What do they think of when it comes to their first foreign language?
What do many people dream of when learning a language?
Who would everyone like to stay in touch with at the end?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I <g>wanted</g> to organize an evening where we all talk about our language biographies. Do you feel like planning that with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first think about what the participants would most like to talk about.
What do you think, Julia?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we ask who each person remembers as having helped them learn a language.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about native languages.
We could ask what people remember when they think of their first foreign language.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we also ask who they learned the most from.
Do you agree with that, Alex?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we also ask what many people dream of when learning a language.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether everyone is ready to answer such personal questions.
Maybe it would be best if we first ask who they're most looking forward to meeting there.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also clarify what people should pay special attention to when telling their story.
Does that work for you, Julia?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we also ask at the end who everyone would like to keep in touch with.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll prepare questions about native languages, first foreign languages, and memories, and at the end we'll ask who everyone would like to stay in touch with. I'm already looking forward to the evening! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You want to plan a mountain hike with a friend until you reach the summit.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare.
These points will help you:
How will you train until you're fit?
What will you wait for before setting off?
How will you practice the route?
What will you do until you reach the goal?
How will you celebrate at the end?

q.en: Hi, David! I want to go hiking in the mountains until we reach the summit. Do you feel like planning that with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we train until we're really fit.
What do you think, Julia?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we wait until the weather gets better before we set off.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the gear.
We could practice the route until we feel confident.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we run every day until we reach our goal.
Do you agree with that, David?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we pack everything until the backpack is fully packed.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can keep up the pace.
Maybe it would be best if we take breaks until we feel strong again.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just keep going until we see the summit, then we'll take a photo.
Does that work for you, Julia?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we celebrate until we're really proud of ourselves.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll train, wait for good weather, and then hike all the way to the summit. At the end we'll celebrate together! I'm already looking forward to the adventure! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: Your new colleague needs help organizing his everyday life here. You want to plan with a colleague how you'll help him.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll do it.
These points will help you:
How does getting up and the start of work function here?
How does commuting to work function?
What's different about working here?
How will you help him with getting to know the neighbours?
What's important for living together?

q.en: Hi, Mark! Our new colleague needs help <g>organizing</g> his everyday life here. Should we plan together how we'll help him?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first talk about getting up, meaning when the workday usually starts here.
What do you think, Nina?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we also explain commuting to him, meaning how the bus and train system works here.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the work itself.
We could explain what makes working different here, for example the break times.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we also help him with getting to know the neighbours.
Do you agree with that, Mark?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we'll show him finding his way around the city with a short walk.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether he already dares to go shopping alone.
Maybe it would be best if we show him how living together with the neighbours works here.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also talk about understanding the local rules, that's often hard at the start.
Does that work for you, Nina?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we also tell him about our own travels through the region, that'll surely make him curious for more.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll explain commuting and working to him, help him with getting to know the neighbours, and show him the city. I'm already looking forward <g>to helping</g> him! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: There are a few misunderstandings in your team. You want to prepare a clarifying conversation with a colleague.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare the conversation.
These points will help you:
What are the colleagues most annoyed about?
How will you prepare for the conversation?
What are some people afraid of?
What does everyone look forward to once the problem is solved?
What should you be able to be proud of at the end?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I think there are a few misunderstandings in the team. Should we prepare a conversation together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first find out what the colleagues are most annoyed about.
What do you think, Alex?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we prepare well for it by writing down all the points beforehand.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the concerns.
We could ask what some colleagues are afraid of.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we talk openly about it, without blaming anyone.
Do you agree with that, Nina?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we also ask what everyone looks forward to once the problem is solved.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether everyone is ready to speak openly.
Maybe it would be best if we first think about how to start the conversation.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just ask at the end what we as a team can really be proud of.
Does that work for you, Alex?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we kindly warn everyone beforehand about it, that it'll be a serious topic.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll find out what everyone's annoyed about, prepare well, and talk openly <g>about it</g>. I'm already looking forward to sorting this out! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You want to write a short etiquette guide for new colleagues with a colleague.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare the guide.
These points will help you:
How do people usually greet each other here?
What topics are okay for small talk, what should be avoided?
What customs and traditions are important to know?
How do you calm someone who feels unsure?
When will the guide be finished?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I was <g>thinking</g> we could write a short etiquette guide for our new colleagues here. Do you feel like planning that with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first explain how people usually greet each other here.
What do you think, Anna?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we also give a few small talk tips, meaning what people like to talk about.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the taboos.
We could make a short list of what to avoid in small talk.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we also explain the most important customs and traditions.
Do you agree with that, Alex?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we also write about how to calm people down who feel unsure at the start.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can fit all the etiquette rules into one document.
Maybe it would be best if we only pick the most important points.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also explain how long it usually takes to get used to everything.
Does that work for you, Anna?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we finish the guide already this week.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll explain the greeting, give small talk tips, and write down the most important customs and traditions. I'm already looking forward to the finished guide! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: A mutual colleague is in the hospital. You want to plan with a colleague how to support her.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll do it.
These points will help you:
When will you visit her at the hospital?
What will you bring?
Who will look after her once she's discharged?
Will you ask the doctor first?
How will you inform other colleagues?

q.en: Hi, David! I <g>heard</g> that Nina is in the hospital. Should we plan together how we'll support her?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we visit her at the hospital tomorrow already.
What do you think, Alex?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we take turns, so that she doesn't get too many visitors every day.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also ask exactly when the visiting hours at the emergency room are.
We could call the clinic beforehand and ask.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we bring her something to read, so she doesn't get bored.
Do you agree with that, David?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: once she's discharged, we take turns looking after her at home.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether she's even allowed visitors yet.
Maybe it would be best if we first ask the doctor whether a visit is okay.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just also inform the other colleagues, so they don't worry unnecessarily.
Does that work for you, Alex?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we write a short message to everyone tonight already.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll ask the doctor, visit her in turns, and look after her at home once she's discharged. I hope she feels better soon! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend Nina has an important examination at the hospital tomorrow. You want to plan with a friend how you'll support her during this time.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner what you'll promise her.
These points will help you:
What will you do as soon as you find out the results?
How often will you visit her?
Will you go with her to therapy?
What will you tell her about the recovery?
What will you promise her for the difficult time?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I talked to the doctor. Nina <g>will have</g> an important examination tomorrow. Should we plan how we'll support her during this time?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we call her as soon as we find out the results.
What do you think, Anna?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we promise her that we will visit her every day.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the therapy.
We could promise that we will go with her to therapy, if she wants that.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we tell her that the pain will subside soon.
Do you agree with that, Alex?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we promise that we will help her through this difficult time.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the diagnosis is already confirmed today.
Maybe it would be best if we say that we will stay flexible, no matter what the doctor says.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just promise that we will never leave her alone.
Does that work for you, Anna?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we tell her that she will surely recover soon.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll call her after the examination, visit her every day, and go with her to therapy. I'm sure she<g>'ll recover</g> soon! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: After an accident last week, you want to organize a first-aid course for the team with a colleague.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare the course.
These points will help you:
What will you practice in the course?
Who should lead the course?
How do you alert help correctly in an emergency?
Theory or practice – what's more important?
When and how often will the course take place?

q.en: Hi, Anna! After the accident last week, I think we should organize a first-aid course for the team. Should we plan that together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we practice how to not only treat wounds but also handle unconscious people.
What do you think, Nina?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we show how to not only stay calm in an emergency but also alert help quickly.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the course instructor.
We could ask someone who has not only experience but also the ability to explain well.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we show how to not only treat a bleeding wound but also recognize shock.
Do you agree with that, Anna?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: we practice not only theoretically but also practically with a dummy.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether enough colleagues will have time.
Maybe it would be best if we offer the course not only once but also a second time.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just bring not only the bandages but also a small handout.
Does that work for you, Nina?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we organize the course already next week, because not only safety but also confidence is important for everyone.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll organize a first-aid course with theory and practice, and practice both wounds and unconsciousness. I'm already looking forward <g>to preparing</g> the team! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: Your brother got hurt and you need to take him to the emergency room. You want to plan with a friend how to organize this.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll proceed.
These points will help you:
What will you bring to register quickly?
What will you do so the waiting time is shorter?
How will you fill out the form?
Who will stay reachable by phone?
What's important so everything is handled urgently?

q.en: Hi, Mark! My brother <g>got hurt</g>, I need to go to the emergency room with him. Can you help me organize that?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that you first take the insurance card, to be able to register quickly.
What do you think, David?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that I fill out the form at home already, to save time.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the waiting time.
We could tell the nurse right away that it's urgent, so that she gives your case priority.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that I sign everything, to not lose any time.
Do you agree with that, Mark?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: I'll call right now, so that the doctors can prepare.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether I can manage everything alone.
Maybe it would be best if I call you, to let you know as soon as we're there.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just hand in the forms together, so that nothing is missing.
Does that work for you, David?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we leave right now, to not lose any more time.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll take the insurance card, fill out the form, and I'll stay reachable by phone. I hope your brother feels better soon! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: A friend's brother needs to have surgery. You want to plan with a friend how to support him.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll proceed.
These points will help you:
How will the surgeon inform the patient?
What questions about anaesthesia and risk should you prepare?
Who will stay during the operation?
How will you find out the prognosis afterwards?
Who will monitor him after the operation?

q.en: Hi, Nina! The doctor said my brother <g>needs to have surgery</g>. Can you help me go through this with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first talk to the surgeon, so that he informs your brother well.
What do you think, David?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we write down all the questions, so that my brother doesn't forget anything.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the risks.
We could ask what risks the anaesthesia carries, so that he really gives informed consent.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that I stay with him, so that he feels calmer before the operation.
Do you agree with that, Nina?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I'd have a suggestion: I'll call you right away, so that you know as soon as the operation is over.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether I can stay calm during the operation.
Maybe it would be best if you're with me, so that I don't have to wait alone.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just stay after the operation, so that the surgeon can tell us the prognosis right away.
Does that work for you, David?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we take turns afterwards, so that someone always monitors him.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll talk to the surgeon, stay with your brother, and wait together for the prognosis. I'm sure everything will go well! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You want to organize a small health day for your team with a colleague.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll prepare the day.
These points will help you:
What's the importance of a health day?
What opportunities will you offer employees?
How will you ensure safety and cleanliness?
What difficulties might arise?
How will you promote health long-term?

q.en: Hi, Julia! I think we should organize a small health day for our team. Should we plan that together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I suggest that we first talk about the importance of health in the workplace.
What do you think, Alex?

q1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we give colleagues the opportunity to have a free check-up.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about safety.
We could also talk about safety at work, for example with heavy lifting.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we also address cleanliness in the kitchen and break rooms.
Do you agree with that, Julia?

a2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
