I'd have a suggestion: we talk openly about the difficulties some people have with stress.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether all colleagues have time that day.
Maybe it would be best if we plan the day so that there's enough freedom in choosing the time.
Would that be okay for you?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just talk at the end about the time after an illness, meaning how to recover well.
Does that work for you, Alex?

q4.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I would suggest that we make our colleagues' health a permanent topic in the team.
Can we agree on that?

a4.en: Yes, good idea! So, we'll talk about health, safety, and cleanliness, offer free check-ups, and plan enough flexibility for everyone. I'm already looking forward to the health day! Talk soon!

task.en:
Situation: You and your neighbour want to do something for the environment on your street together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What? (clean-up campaign by the river)
When? (date, time)
What to bring? (gloves, garbage bags)
How often to repeat it?
Who else to invite?

q.en: Hi, Anna! We <g>wanted</g> to organize something for the environment in our street together, didn't we?

a.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
I have a suggestion: we could organize a clean-up campaign by the river to do something for the environment.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the date.
How about we do that on Saturday morning?
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could bring gloves and garbage bags.
Do you have a better idea?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we not only do this once, but repeat it with a fixed frequency, for example once a month.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how many neighbors will actually take part.
My suggestion would be that we try it every two months at first, so that the action stays sustainable.
Would that be okay for you?

q3.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
Let's also invite the children from the neighborhood, so they develop more awareness for the environment.
Can we agree on that?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure.
Maybe it would be best if we inform the property management about the action first.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
One idea would be that we buy a few extra garbage bags in case there's a shortage.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: on Saturday we'll meet by the river, bring gloves and garbage bags, and invite the children too. That's really a nice action for more sustainability on our street. See you Saturday, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: You and your roommate want to save energy in your apartment together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What first? (light, heating)
How to save? (switching off, insulating)
Renewable energy sources?
Who checks what?
How often to review?

q.en: Hi, Anna! I <g>noticed</g> that our energy consumption is quite high. Should we plan together how we can save energy?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: electricity is saved when we use less light in the evening.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the windows.
We could first make sure the windows are insulated.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we make sure the light is switched off when nobody is in the room.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that the apartment is heated two degrees less in winter, to save energy.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether we won't be cold then.
One idea would be that we also use renewable energy sources in the long term, so they are used more often.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
How about we find out how a solar panel system is installed on our roof?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether that's affordable for us.
Maybe it would be best if we first check how our energy consumption is monitored every month.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
One idea would be that we make a small list, so that nothing is wasted anymore.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll switch off the light, insulate the windows, heat more economically, and find out about solar panels and renewable energy. That way we'll really save energy! Thanks for the good planning, David!

task.en:
Situation: You and your colleague want to organize an action for more environmental awareness in your team together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What have you already done?
What is planned next?
Who do you want to convince?
How do you want to measure success?
Who advocates for what?

q.en: Hi, Julia! Shall we think together about how we can make our team even more environmentally conscious?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: for example, I've already avoided a lot of plastic – we could do that across the whole team.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the energy.
We could suggest switching to a green energy provider at the office – at home we've already switched.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we show our colleagues that demand for green energy has risen sharply in recent years.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we document that our plastic use in the office has already decreased since we started using reusable cups.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify exactly how we measure that.
One idea would be that we keep going – I've already convinced some colleagues to separate their waste.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we find more colleagues who, like me, have advocated for environmental protection?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether everyone will join in.
Maybe it would be best if we first show that we've already reduced our plastic waste as a team, before setting bigger goals.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's explain that to everyone on the team – I've realized myself that everyone can contribute something.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll tell our colleagues what we've already achieved, convince more people to separate waste, and keep advocating for the environment. This will definitely be a great campaign! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to spend a day volunteering together on an organic farm.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What tasks? (planting, feeding, irrigation)
How do you help with the sale? (marketing, packaging, delivery)
What else interests you? (breeding, fertilizing)
What to bring?
Who else to ask?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I <g>heard</g> about an organic farm nearby that's looking for volunteers. Should we help out there together for a day?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we could help with the planting of vegetables, that fits the season well.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the fertilizing.
We could also help with that, in case they need help there.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also take care of the irrigation of the beds if it's very dry.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we join the feeding of the animals in the morning, I find that really interesting.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how long we'll stay.
One idea would be that we also ask how the marketing of the products works.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also help with the delivery of the vegetable boxes to the customers?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll have time for that.
Maybe it would be best if we first help with the packaging of the boxes and do the delivery later.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also ask the farmers about the breeding of new vegetable varieties, that sounds exciting.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll help with planting, fertilizing and watering, feed the animals, pack the boxes and ask about marketing and breeding. This will definitely be a great day! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: You and your colleague want to plan a trip to a farm with the children from your class.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What will you show the children? (sowing, harvesting, mowing, milking)
How do you check that everything is safe?
What will the children learn about recycling and deposit bottles?
How is the waste sorted?
What else to bring?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I have an idea: shall we plan a trip to a farm with our class?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we could show the children how the vegetables are sown.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the season.
We could also show how the fruit is harvested, that fits well into autumn right now.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also ask if we can watch how the cows are milked.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that the children also see how the meadow for the animals is mowed.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how we handle safety.
One idea would be that we ask beforehand how often the animals are checked there.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also ask how the vegetables are sorted after the harvest?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the children will find that interesting.
Maybe it would be best if we also show them how the waste is separated on the farm.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also give the children deposit bottles, so they can see how they are collected at the end.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: the children will see how sowing, harvesting and mowing is done, how the cows are milked, and how waste and deposit bottles are sorted. That will be a great and educational trip! Thanks for the idea, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to organize an information event about climate change together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What do you want to inform people about? (climate crisis, global warming, CO2 emissions)
How do you want to raise people's awareness?
What can people do sustainably?
Who do you invite?
Where and when does the event take place?

q.en: Hi, Mark! I want to do something about the climate crisis. Should we plan an information event about climate change together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we could first talk about global warming and CO2 emissions, because many people still don't really understand that.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the causes.
We could also explain what actually causes climate change, for example traffic and industry.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also talk about the effects, for example on animals and nature.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we show people how their own behavior influences the climate.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much time we have for that.
One idea would be that we also give practical tips on how to live more sustainably.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also explain how each individual can protect the environment?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll have enough time to explain everything.
Maybe it would be best if we invite an expert to create more awareness of the topic.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's ask an expert whether they can come on Friday evening.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll inform people about global warming, CO2 emissions and the effects, give tips for a sustainable life, and invite an expert. That way we'll create more awareness of the climate crisis! Thanks for the idea, Julia!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to attend an art event together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
When does the event take place? (date)
Where? (venue)
How do you register? (registration)
Do you need an invitation?
Do you need to ask for permission?

q.en: Hi, Julia! I <g>heard</g> that a great art event is taking place at the museum. Shall we go together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: let's first find out on which date the event takes place.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the location.
We could also check exactly where the venue is, so that we don't arrive too late.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we both register online, because registration is required.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we also ask whether we can invite another friend, then we might get a second invitation.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how many people can come along.
One idea would be that we both ask for permission at work, since the event already starts in the afternoon.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we read a bit about the art there beforehand, so we understand more?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether there are still spots available.
Maybe it would be best if we register today already, before all the spots are gone.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's register together right now, then we'll definitely have a spot.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll both register now, ask for permission at work, and read a bit about the art. I'm already looking forward to the event! Thanks for the invitation, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to attend a festival together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What do you need to prepare for?
What do you take care of? (tickets)
What do you need to think about?
What can you rely on?
What do you need to get used to?

q.en: Hi, Mark! The festival is already in a week! Shall we plan together what we still need to do?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we should first prepare well for the festival and make a list.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the tickets.
We could first take care of the tickets, before they're sold out.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we remember the earplugs in time, otherwise we'll forget them again.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we also think about the weather and pack a jacket in case it rains.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how we'll get there.
One idea would be that we still wait for the confirmation from the ticket sellers before we plan everything else.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we rely on my brother? He can drive us there.
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether he really has time.
Maybe it would be best if we deal with the trip ourselves and maybe take a train.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's slowly get used to camping and spend a night in the garden first.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll prepare for the festival, take care of the tickets, remember the earplugs and think about the weather. I'm already really looking forward to it! Thanks for the planning, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend were at the festival together and now want to write a review about it together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What are you proud of?
What do you want to complain about?
What were you disappointed by?
What do you remember most?
What are you curious about?

q.en: Hi, David! I want to write a review about the festival together with you. <g>What</g> are you most proud of when you look back?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: I'm really proud of that – that we stayed in a good mood the whole time despite the rain – we could write that first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the criticism.
We could also write about what some people complained about, for example the long queues.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also write that we briefly complained about that – that the food was so expensive.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we also mention what we were maybe a little disappointed by.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how honest we want to be.
One idea would be that we honestly write that I was only a little disappointed by that – that the stage was so far away.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also write about what we'll remember the longest?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can fit everything into one text.
Maybe it would be best if we write that I'll definitely remember that the longest – how great the mood was on the last evening.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also write at the end what we're already curious about for the next festival.
Are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll write about our experience, our impression, what we're proud of, what we complained about, and what we're already looking forward to. I'm really looking forward to writing the text with you! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to become members of the city library together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do you become a member? (card, fee)
Which books do you want to reserve?
How long is the deadline?
What do you do if you want to extend the deadline?
How do you return the books?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I <g>heard</g> that the city library has a great program. Shall we become members together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we could go together and both get a library card.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the costs.
We could ask beforehand whether there's a fee for the membership.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also reserve a few books online right away, so that they're already waiting for us.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we note right away how long the deadline for returning is, so we don't forget anything.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how often you're allowed to keep the books.
One idea would be that we also ask whether you can extend the deadline online, in case we need more time.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also check whether the library sends a message before the deadline ends?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll always manage that in time.
Maybe it would be best if we return the books together instead, then neither of us will forget.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's be registered as members already tomorrow and pick up our first books.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: tomorrow we'll get a library card, reserve books, note the deadline, and return everything together. I'm already looking forward to our new member adventure! Thanks for the idea, Julia!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to take part in a library tour together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
When is the tour? (opening hours)
Does admission cost anything?
What else do you want to ask? (catalogue, collection, reading room)
Who do you ask? (staff member)
What else do you want to look at?

q.en: Hi, David! I <g>heard</g> that the library offers a guided tour. Shall we go together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: let's first check the opening hours, so we know when the tour takes place.
So, what do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the admission.
We could also ask whether there's a fee for the tour.
How do you actually find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also have the reading room shown to us and ask how you can borrow books there.
Are you actually okay with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we also ask about the quiet area, in case we ever want to study there.
So, how do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how long the tour lasts.
One idea would be that we also have the special collection of old books shown to us.
What do you actually think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also ask how the digital catalogue works, so we can find books more easily?
So, does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can ask that many questions at once.
Maybe it would be best if we write down a few questions beforehand and then ask a staff member.
Actually, what's your take on that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's sign up for the next tour right away, then we'll have everything sorted out.
So, are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll check the opening hours, ask about the admission fee, look at the reading room and the collection, and sign up for the tour. I'm already looking forward to it! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to visit a graffiti exhibition together and talk to the artists.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
Which exhibition do you visit?
Do you also want to take part in an action yourselves?
Who can you recommend?
What do you want to exchange views with the artists about?
What's important or unimportant to you at the event?

q.en: Hi, Anna! I <g>heard</g> about a graffiti exhibition. Shall we go together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: I read that a still unknown artist is also showing his artworks there – that sounds exciting.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the permission.
We could ask beforehand, because I'm unsure whether you're also allowed to spray there yourself.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also ask a staff member directly, because the rules on the website were quite unclear to me.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we get a few artists recommended to us beforehand, because it's impossible to see all the artworks in one day.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much time we'll spend there.
One idea would be that we only look at the most important works, since the exact order is actually unimportant.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we still dare to talk to the artists, even if some might react a bit unfriendly?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether everyone will like that.
Maybe it would be best if we ask someone else too, because I find street art really exciting, but for others the topic might be uninteresting.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just give it a try, even if it's a bit untypical for both of us to take part in something like this.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll visit the exhibition, have artists recommended to us, ask about the rules, and exchange views with the artists. This will definitely be exciting! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend both want to change jobs and are planning together how to apply.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What would your dream job be?
What would you wish for regarding the salary?
Who could help with the cover letter?
What would be important to you at work? (flexible hours, nice colleagues)
How would you prepare for an interview?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I <g>heard</g> that you're also thinking about switching jobs. Shall we plan together how to apply?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: I would love to work at a company with flexible hours – let's search for that first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the salary.
We could also talk about that – if only I had a higher salary, I could afford more.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also talk about the industry – I would most love to switch to the IT industry.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we also think about what a promotion could look like – I would love to get a promotion this year too.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how realistic that is.
One idea would be that we first work on the overtime – I really would love to work fewer overtime hours.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we help each other with the cover letter? It would be nice if we both had a new position soon.
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether I'm ready for an interview yet.
Maybe it would be best if we practice a little first – I would wish that the new colleagues are at least nice.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's meet tomorrow – I would love your help with the cover letter.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll search for flexible positions, talk about the salary and the promotion, help each other with the cover letter, and practice for the interview. I'm already looking forward to our new careers! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your colleague both dream of a new job and want to plan together how you'll apply.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What would you do if you had more time?
Where do you find job ads?
What would you change in your CV?
How would you show more motivation?
What would be your chance at the dream job?

q.en: Hi, Anna! I <g>heard</g> that you're also dreaming of a new job. Shall we plan together how we can apply?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: if I had more time, I would search new job ads every day – let's do that together.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the courage.
We could be honest – if I were braver, I would quit right away, but maybe we should find a new job first.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we help each other – if I updated my CV, I would surely have better chances.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we set ourselves goals – if I applied to more companies, I would also have more opportunities.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much time we really have.
One idea would be that we think about part-time work – if I could work part-time, I would have more time for applications.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we motivate each other? If I had more motivation, I would apply today already.
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether a new job really makes everything better.
Maybe it would be best if we first think about what's important to us – if the employer were more flexible, I would already be much more satisfied.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's support each other. If we both had our dream job, we would both be much happier.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll search for job ads, update our CVs, apply to several companies, and motivate each other. I'm already looking forward to our chance! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend are both preparing your job application documents and want to support each other.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What are you hoping for?
What are you counting on?
What are you convinced of?
What are you looking forward to?
What are you worried about?

q.en: Hi, Julia! We're both writing our applications right now. Shall we help each other?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: I hope that we both get feedback quickly – let's finish the documents together.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about reality.
We could also count on the fact that not every application works out right away.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we stay positive – I'm convinced that we have good chances.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we focus on the positive – I'm already looking forward to the fact that we'll have the interview soon.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much time we have left.
One idea would be that we are honest – I'm worried that we won't have all the documents ready in time.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we clarify that first? It really annoys me that my certificate is still missing.
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether that's so important right now.
Maybe it would be best if we first keep in mind that we need to impress the HR manager.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also make sure that the home-office question is mentioned in the cover letter.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll prepare the documents, take care of the certificate and the home-office question, and stay positive. I'm already looking forward to the feedback! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend both have a job interview coming up soon and want to prepare together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
Which questions do you practice?
How do you talk about strengths and weaknesses?
What are your expectations?
How do you want to react if a question is difficult?
How important is your demeanour?

q.en: Hi, David! We both have a job interview coming up soon. Shall we practice together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: let's start with an important question – for example: 'Why do you want to work here?'
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the weaknesses.
We could also practice how to stay calm with a difficult question, for example a question about weaknesses.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we take a calm moment before every answer, before we speak.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we show the company that it's finding an independent employee in us.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how we react to criticism.
One idea would be that we also practice how to react calmly and politely to a critical question.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we look at a typical example from the internet, so we know what to expect?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether that's enough.
Maybe it would be best if we also talk about practical experience we've already gained.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's tell each other that this is a brave step for both of us.
Are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll practice important and difficult questions, talk about our strengths and experience, and stay calm and brave. I'm already looking forward to the interview! Thanks for the idea, Julia!

task.en:
Situation: You and your colleague want to introduce new habits together for a better everyday work life.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How can you take real breaks?
How do you manage to leave work on time?
What would you change about your workplace?
What further training would make sense?
What are your wishes, and what is reality?

q.en: Hi, Mark! I <g>noticed</g> that neither of us ever really takes a break. Shall we introduce new habits for our everyday work life together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we could introduce a fixed break where we really step away from the screen.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the end of the workday.
We could also aim to leave work on time, instead of always staying longer.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also tidy up our workplace, so that we can concentrate better.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we both pursue further training regularly, so we can take on more responsibility.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much time that takes.
One idea would be that we talk honestly about the wage, because our wishes and reality sometimes don't match up.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we develop a fixed habit of talking about the week every Friday?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll manage that every week.
Maybe it would be best if we first look at how satisfied we are working in our current position.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's start with the first real break tomorrow already.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll take real breaks, leave work on time, tidy up the workplace, and pursue further training. I'm already looking forward to our new everyday routine! Thanks for the idea, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend are both taking part in a competition and want to prepare together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do you warm up?
How do you stretch?
How do you check the equipment?
How do you concentrate before it starts?
How do you deal with nervousness?

q.en: Hi, Alex! We both have a competition coming up soon. Shall we plan together how we'll prepare?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we should warm up well before the competition begins.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the equipment.
We could check it before we go to the starting line.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we stretch properly before we really get started.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that I concentrate calmly before the competition starts.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how we deal with nervousness.
One idea would be that we take a few deep breaths before we get too nervous.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we are on time before we have to stand at the starting line?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll remember that.
Maybe it would be best if we drink enough before we really push ourselves.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also move around a bit before our muscles get cold.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll warm up, check the equipment, stretch, concentrate, and move around lightly. I'm already looking forward to the competition! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your teammate have gotten a new coach and want to plan together how the new team gets off to a good start.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do you welcome the new coach?
What tactics do you suggest?
How do you show your talent?
What success do you want to achieve?
How do you deal with the new challenge?

q.en: Hi, Nina! We have a new coach now. Shall we plan together how the new team can get off to a good start?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: the new coach is arriving tomorrow already – let's welcome him together.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the team.
We could imagine what it's like when a new coach gets to know a team – we should be open and friendly.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we show him right away what the great talent of our team is.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we also say that each of us brings a great talent.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much we already know.
One idea would be that we ask what the new tactics will look like, before we plan too much.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we firmly resolve to achieve a great success together?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we should promise that right at the start.
Maybe it would be best if we first show that we can repeat the good performance from last season.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's say together that this season is a big challenge for all of us.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll welcome the new coach, show our talent, ask about the tactics, and take on the challenge together. I'm already looking forward to the new season! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend are both taking part in a championship and want to train and prepare together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
Which route do you choose?
What pace do you run?
Who is the strongest opponent?
What time is your goal?
How do you train your endurance?

q.en: Hi, Julia! We're both taking part in the championship. Shall we train together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: let's choose a faster route for our training than last time.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the competition day.
We could find out beforehand which is the fastest route on the competition day.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we try out a higher pace than usual during training.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we only run the highest pace at the end of the route, so we don't get tired too early.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify who the competition is.
One idea would be that we find out who the stronger opponent in our group might be.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we prepare especially for the strongest opponent, so we're not afraid of him?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we should focus too much on the opponent.
Maybe it would be best if we simply focus on a better time than last time.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's both aim together to run the best time of our lives.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll choose a faster route, train our pace, prepare for the strongest opponent, and run for a better time. I'm already looking forward to the championship! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: You and your colleague want to organize a charity run for a good cause together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do you find volunteers and participants?
Which route do you choose?
How do you collect donations?
Who receives the proceeds?
How do you convince the club to support it?

q.en: Hi, Anna! I want to organize a charity run. Shall we plan it together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we'll definitely need more volunteers to help us organize.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the number of participants.
We could ask more people – I already asked an acquaintance whether he'll take part as a runner.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we plan two routes, one for children and a longer one for adults.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we try out something new this year, for example online registration.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify what amount we expect.
One idea would be that we use the proceeds for the best thing for the club – for example new equipment.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we donate the money instead to those in need in our city, for example a clinic?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the club will agree to that.
Maybe it would be best if we both ask – last year even a stranger spontaneously donated, so the support is definitely there.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's transfer the amount at the end to an organization for the sick in our region.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll look for volunteers, plan the route, collect donations, and give the proceeds to the sick. I'm already looking forward to the charity run! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to make suggestions together about how your friends could move more.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What sport do you suggest?
How do you convince the others?
Who do you persuade first?
How do you gradually improve everyone's fitness?
Do you want to organize an event?

q.en: Hi, Nina! Our friends move way too little. Shall we come up with some suggestions about sport together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we could suggest a completely new type of sport, for example climbing.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the costs.
We could first think about how to best convince the others.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we persuade Mark first, because he usually gets the others to join too.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we start slowly, so everyone can improve their fitness without pressure.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify when we have time.
One idea would be that we organize a small event where everyone can simply try out the new sport.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also ask whether we can work together with a local club?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether everyone really wants to join in.
Maybe it would be best if we hold a small record challenge, so it's more fun for everyone.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's talk to Mark tomorrow already and suggest the whole idea to him.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll suggest a new sport, persuade Mark first, organize a small event, and look for a club. I'm already looking forward to it! Thanks for the idea, Julia!

task.en:
Situation: You and your partner are expecting a child and want to prepare for the birth together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do you find a midwife?
When does maternity leave begin?
Who takes paternity leave?
What do you need for the newborn?
How do you find a daycare spot?

q.en: Hi, Mark! The pregnancy is already entering its final phase. Shall we prepare for the birth together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we should first find a midwife who can accompany us during the birth.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about maternity protection.
We could also clarify exactly when my maternity leave begins, so I stop working in time.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also talk to my boss about paternity leave already.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we buy a stroller and other things for the newborn together.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much money we have for that.
One idea would be that we discuss now how we'll take turns with breastfeeding and changing nappies.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we register for a daycare spot already now, since the waiting lists are so long?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we should plan that far ahead already.
Maybe it would be best if we just take our time and take on the responsibility step by step.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's still call the midwife this week, then we'll have the most important thing done.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll look for a midwife, clarify the maternity and paternity leave, buy a stroller, and register for a daycare spot. I'm already looking forward to our newborn! Thanks for the idea, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend raises his child alone and often doesn't want to ask for help. You want to build a system together so he doesn't have to do everything alone.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What can you help with?
How do you show that there's no need to be ashamed?
How do you share the responsibility?
How do you manage everyday life together?
Why is there no need to prove anything?

q.en: Hi, David! I <g>noticed</g> that you're trying to manage everything on your own. Shall we plan together how I can help you?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: you're right – I really don't need to do everything alone, even if it sometimes feels that way.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about your feelings.
We could keep reminding ourselves: you don't need to be ashamed when you ask for help.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we tell each other: we don't need to worry when we can rely on each other.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that you know: you don't need to carry the responsibility alone, because I'm always here.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how often I'm allowed to call.
One idea would be that we agree: I don't need to hesitate to just call you when I need help.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we divide the tasks? For example, you don't always need to do the shopping alone.
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether I can really accept that.
Maybe it would be best if we make it clear to ourselves: we don't need to prove anything to each other.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just start doing this together from now on: you don't need to cope with everyday life alone anymore.
Are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: I'll call you when I need help, we'll share the responsibility and everyday life, and I won't be ashamed to ask for help anymore. Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your partner are expecting a child and want to plan together how to divide the household, childcare, and work.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
Who works while the other stays at home?
How do you split the housework?
Who looks after the child while the other works?
How do you take turns with parental leave?
What do you think about traditional men's roles?

q.en: Hi, Alex! Our child is coming soon. Shall we plan together how we'll divide the housework and childcare?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: while you cook, I can play with the child – that way we both have something to do.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the working hours.
We could also decide: while you're working, I'll look after the child, and the other way around.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also take turns with the shopping: while I'm working from home, you can go shopping.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we take turns with the housework: while you do the housework, I'll check on the baby.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how long the parental leave lasts.
One idea would be that we take turns with parental leave: while one of us stays at home, the other works.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we deliberately show: while some people still believe in old man's roles, we'd rather split everything equally?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can always split everything exactly equally.
Maybe it would be best if we organize ourselves flexibly: while you take care of the upbringing, I'll handle the calls and appointments.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's just try it that way: while the child is sleeping, we can relax together.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll share the housework, upbringing and work, take turns with parental leave, and leave old role models behind. I'm already looking forward to our life as a family of three! Thanks for the idea, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: You and your partner want to think together about how to raise your children without old women's and men's roles.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do you react to stereotypes and prejudices?
How do you split the tasks at home?
What role models do you show the children?
How do you accept differences between the children?
How do you talk about equality?

q.en: Hi, Mark! I want our kids to grow up without old women's and men's roles. Shall we plan that together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: maybe someone in our family still thinks in old stereotypes – we should calmly address that.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the prejudices.
We could agree: no one should tell our kids what boys or girls are allowed to do and what not.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we show the children something important: that boys are allowed to cry too and girls are allowed to be angry too.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we make sure our children don't pick up anything from these old prejudices.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify who takes which task.
One idea would be that we divide the tasks clearly – this task here is mine, we'll share the other one.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we agree right away: doing the laundry is yours, I'll do the cooking.
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether our son already understands that.
Maybe it would be best if we simply show him: if he wants a doll, that's his, just like a ball.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's do the same with our daughter: if she wants to play football, that's hers, just like dancing.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll talk about stereotypes, share the tasks fairly, and accept that each child has their own interests. I'm already looking forward to more equality in our family! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: You and your ex-partner have separated and want to plan together how your child can feel comfortable in both apartments.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What does your child need in both apartments?
How do you set up a room for your child?
What do you pack for switching between the houses?
How do you talk about custody?
How do you help your child feel comfortable in the new blended family?

q.en: Hi, Julia! Now that we've separated, we should think about how our child can feel comfortable in both homes. Shall we plan that together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: we could pack a small suitcase that always travels with her between the apartments.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about her own room.
We could also set up a proper little room for her at my place, not just a corner.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we buy a cozy little bed for her, so she sleeps well everywhere.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we maybe even give her a little kitten that lives at my place – that could help her.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify who takes care of the animal.
One idea would be that we first hang a little picture of our whole family in both rooms, so she feels connected.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we put a small little table for drawing in both rooms for her?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we need that much furniture already.
Maybe it would be best if we first put a simple little basket for her favorite toys in each room.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also buy her a little dollhouse to play with, that can stay at my place.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll both set up a little room, pack a little suitcase, hang up a little picture, and make sure she feels comfortable in our blended family. I'm already looking forward to it! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend recently came to Germany and want to plan the next steps for your professional future together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do you apply for recognition of your qualification?
Which language course do you take?
How do you settle in?
Which applications do you need to submit to which authorities?
Who helps you with translating?

q.en: Hi, Anna! <g>Now that we've both arrived here</g>, we should think about how things continue professionally. Shall we plan that together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: now that we've arrived here, we should first apply for recognition of our qualifications, so our training gets recognised.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about our language skills.
We could also take a language course – now that I've already attended a course, I feel much more confident.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we take time to integrate well: now that we've settled in, we can concentrate much better on work.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we go to the authority together: now that you've already been there once, you know which documents we need.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how long that takes.
One idea would be that we submit the application already today: now that we've submitted the application, we just need to wait.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we ask our friend: now that he's translated the documents, we can submit them right away?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we've understood everything yet.
Maybe it would be best if we remember: after we had gotten our bearings at the start, we found everything much easier, so it'll work out this time too.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also keep in mind: after we had found the apartment, everything really went much faster afterwards.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll apply for recognition, take a language course, go to the authority, and have the documents translated. I'm already looking forward to our new start! Thanks for the idea, Julia!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to update your CVs together and talk about your previous work experience.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What had you already done before you came here?
Which company had you already managed or founded?
Which degree had you already completed?
Which position had you already held?
What had you already studied?

q.en: Hi, David! We should update our CVs. Shall we do that together and talk about our previous experience?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: before I came here, I had already gained ten years of experience on the labour market – I should definitely mention that.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the order.
We could start with that: after I had written my CV for the first time, I felt much more confident.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
My suggestion would be that we also mention: before I got this job, I had already founded my own company.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we also write: when I arrived here, I had already managed a large team.
How do you see it?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how many details we write.
One idea would be that we clearly highlight the degree: before I came to Germany, I had already finished my degree.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also explain: after I had studied economics, I switched to a completely different industry?
Does that work for you?

a3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether that's important for the new job.
Maybe it would be best if we mention it anyway: before I had this position, I had already worked at three different companies.
What do you think about that?

q4.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's write at the end: when I applied, I had already gained so much experience that I was very confident.
Are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll write about our labour market experience, our companies, our degree, and our positions. I'm already looking forward to the new CVs! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: You and your colleague want to organise a training session for new employees together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
What do we organise first? (topics, schedule)
Who coordinates the appointments with the other departments?
Who presents which topic and who documents the results?
How do we delegate the remaining tasks?
Who decides about the room and the materials?

q.en: Hi, David! We're supposed to organise a training session for the new colleagues together. Shall we start planning right away?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: Organising the topics should be our first step, then we can plan a clear schedule.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the schedule.
We could clarify that first: Planning the schedule is the next step, and then we divide the topics between two mornings.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
My suggestion would be that we leave coordinating the appointments with the other departments to me, because I already have contact with the works council.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we split up the presenting like this: I take over presenting the practical topics, and you explain the theory?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify who gets the remaining tasks.
One idea would be that we leave delegating the smaller tasks to the new colleagues in training – that would also be good practice for them.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether that's fair for everyone.
Maybe it would be best if deciding about the room and the materials happens together, so that everyone can agree.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's do it this way: I'll take over documenting the results at the end of every session, so we'll have everything in writing.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
I suggest that we don't forget listening to the participants' feedback at the end, in order to improve the training next time.
Are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: I'll take care of the coordination and the documentation, you take over the organising and the presenting, and we'll delegate the smaller tasks together to the new colleagues. At the end, we'll listen carefully to the feedback. I'm already looking forward to the training! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: You and your colleague want to help a mutual friend who wants to start a vocational training.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.
These points will help you:
How do we check her school-leaving qualification and organise a student internship?
How do we help her prepare for the exam?
How do we explain the process and the transition between school and the company to her?
What do we need to pay attention to regarding the employment contract?
How do we support her further training and satisfaction in the new job?

q.en: Hi, Anna! Our friend wants to start a vocational training. Shall we plan together how we can support her with that?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: First we check her school-leaving qualification and suggest a student internship to her, because luckily this job is easy to learn.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about her free time.
We could pick out a few doable tasks together that she can take on during the internship.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we help her study for the exam, so that she passes it as flawlessly as possible.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we write down the process for the first few weeks together, so that everything runs smoothly?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how she organises herself between school and the company.
One idea would be that we give her a few tips for a problem-free transition between vocational school and the company.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether she can still afford all that alongside the training.
Maybe it would be best if we show her that there are also free further training offers.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's read through the employment contract together, so that every point is easily understandable for her.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we ask her at the end how satisfied she is with the new job – that will undoubtedly give her more confidence for the start.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, here's what we'll do: we'll help her with the school-leaving qualification and the student internship, practise with her for the exam, explain the process and the employment contract to her, and at the end we'll ask about her satisfaction. I'm already looking forward to helping her! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend wants his foreign qualification to be recognised in Germany, and you want to help him with that.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll proceed.
These points will help you:
What proof does he need for his qualification?
Does his job profile match a German training occupation?
Does he need a work permit first?
Can a trade union help him?
How can he officially use his title?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I <g>heard</g> that you want to get your qualification from your home country recognised here. Shall we plan together how you can best proceed?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: First I should gather all the proof of my training, so certificates and diplomas.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about your job profile.
We could check whether it matches a German training occupation exactly, that's important for the recognition.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also clarify whether I already need a work permit before I apply.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we get information from a trade union? They can help you with questions about labour law.
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how long the assessment of my qualification takes.
One idea would be that we ask the responsible office about it directly.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether you're allowed to simply keep using your title here.
Maybe it would be best if we check that carefully before you use it on your documents.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also check whether the procedure works the same everywhere within Germany, or whether there are differences outside my federal state.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we think at the end about how you can successfully get established here as a new employee.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, first we gather my proof of qualifications, check my job profile and the work permit, get information from the trade union, clarify my qualification and my title, and check whether there are differences within or outside my federal state. Then nothing will stand in the way of my success as an employee! Thanks for your help, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: After a flood in the region, you and your friend want to help voluntarily.
Task: Plan your volunteer work together with your conversation partner.
These points will help you:
What needs to be done first?
Which tools need to be repaired?
How should donations be collected and distributed?
What else needs to be obtained?
How can the volunteer work be planned well?

q.en: Hi, Julia! After the flood, many people want to help voluntarily. Shall we plan together how we can get involved?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: First the animals in the flooded basements need to be rescued.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the tools.
We could first clarify which tools are damaged – they need to be repaired right away.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also keep in mind: clothes and food need to be collected before we set off.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also think about this: the donations need to be distributed fairly, so that every family gets something?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how many helpers we need in total.
One idea would be that we make a list: the route needs to be planned carefully in advance, so we don't lose any time.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can manage all that in one day.
Maybe it would be best if we set some deadlines: these tasks need to be done by tomorrow morning, otherwise we'll be too late.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also check what else needs to be obtained, for example gloves and buckets.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we officially register for the voluntary position at the end, so that our voluntary work is also properly organised.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, first we rescue the animals, repair the tools, collect clothes and food, distribute the donations fairly, plan the route carefully, get everything done by tomorrow morning, and obtain gloves and buckets. And of course we'll officially register for the voluntary position! I'm already looking forward to it! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to get involved as volunteers together, but there are some challenges.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll manage despite the obstacles.
These points will help you:
How can you get involved despite illness or disability?
What do you do differently because of the pandemic?
When do you have time during the holidays?
How do you deal with the shortage of helpers?
What do you do in bad weather?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I'd like to get involved as a volunteer, but I don't know yet exactly how that works best. Shall we plan it together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: Because of the pandemic, many organisations now also offer online volunteering, we could try that first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about our health.
We could keep in mind: despite an illness, you don't have to stay home, there are also lighter tasks.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we start right away during the holidays, then we'll have more time.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we register specifically? Because of the shortage of helpers, new volunteers are surely being sought.
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify what happens in bad weather.
One idea would be that we keep going outside despite the bad weather, if we dress warmly enough.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether that's doable for everyone.
Maybe it would be best if we also keep in mind that some people want to get involved despite a disability – so we should also offer accessible tasks.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also make a plan for who of the two of us fills in during an appointment, in case one of us can't make it.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we put you forward as the contact person, because due to your experience you know the most about it.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we'll start during the holidays, offer lighter tasks despite illness or disability, also do online volunteering because of the pandemic, keep working despite bad weather, and register as volunteers right away because of the shortage of helpers. I'm already looking forward to our volunteer work! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to advocate for more tolerance in your neighbourhood.
Task: Plan a project for this together with your conversation partner.
These points will help you:
How can you make use of the neighbours' commitment?
Who can give a donation for the project?
Which organisations can help with the initiative?
How can you honour each person's contribution?
How do you document the project?

q.en: Hi, Julia! I'd like to advocate for more tolerance in our neighbourhood. Shall we plan a project together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: Because of the great commitment of many neighbours, we could first organise a small street festival.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the costs.
We could keep in mind: despite the great effort the festival requires, it's definitely worth it for the community spirit.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we get started right away, because thanks to the generous donation from Mrs Meier, we already have a bit of starting capital.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also reach out to other clubs during this exciting initiative, so that even more people join in?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify who takes care of the registration.
One idea would be that we invite everyone personally because of their important contribution, then everyone feels included.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether a small organisation can manage that alone.
Maybe it would be best if we work together with the neighbourhood association instead, despite our small organisation.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also take photos right away during the new project, so we can report about it later.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we say thank you at the end because of the quick help from the neighbourhood association.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, because of the great commitment of many neighbours we'll organise the street festival, thanks to the donation we have starting capital, we'll work together with other associations, and we'll personally invite everyone because of their contribution. That way we can promote more tolerance in the neighbourhood together! I'm already looking forward to our initiative! Thanks for the idea, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to organise a helpful circle of friends in which everyone supports each other.
Task: Plan this together with your conversation partner.
These points will help you:
Which areas of mutual help are important?
What support services can you offer?
How do you show empathy and consideration?
How do you ensure a respectful atmosphere?
How does the circle of friends become successful?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I have an idea: we could organise a circle of friends where we all help each other. Shall we plan that together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: A sensible first step would be to define different areas where we can help each other, for example shopping or childcare.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about empathy.
We could offer loving support, especially when someone has health problems.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we agree on a considerate way of dealing with each other, so that no one feels overwhelmed.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also create a support service for new members? That makes me really hopeful for the future of our circle.
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how we find new members.
One idea would be that we establish a respectful tone in the group, so that everyone feels safe asking for help.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can all manage that time-wise.
Maybe it would be best if we give each other strong support, even when someone has little time.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also check later whether our circle of friends is really successful, and then maybe invite even more people.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we put together all the areas and support services in a list with a lot of empathy at the end, so that everyone knows where to find support.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we define sensible areas, offer loving support, treat each other considerately, create a support service for new members, make sure the tone is respectful, give each other strong support, and check whether our circle is successful. With a lot of empathy, that will definitely be great! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: David and Julia are considering whether and how they want to get involved as volunteers together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll put this into practice.
These points will help you:
What dangers should you keep in mind?
What support can you get?
How do you build trust in the new task?
Which day do you set aside for it?
What value does this work have for you?
