q.en: Hi, Julia! I've been thinking for a while about getting involved as a volunteer. Shall we think together about how to do that best?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We could ask our whole circle of friends, then we can stick together and motivate each other.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the danger.
We could say: on the one hand there are certainly exciting tasks, on the other hand we definitely shouldn't do anything too dangerous.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we first get information from an organisation that supports us with the first steps.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we try out a small project first, so that we build trust in our new task?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how much time we really have.
One idea would be that we set aside a fixed day each week for our idea, then it will really become a habit.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we'll keep it up long enough.
Maybe it would be best if we remind each other what value this work has for other people, then we'll stay motivated.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also ask our friends right away whether they want to join, so that we stick together as a circle of friends.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also think at the end about how we organise our support in the long term.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we ask our circle of friends, find out about the dangers and the tasks, get support from an organisation, try out a small project, set aside a fixed day, and always remember the value of our work. That way we can really stick together and build trust! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: A new neighbour has moved into your apartment building.
Task: Plan together with your neighbour how you'll welcome him.
These points will help you:
Who from the building do you invite to get to know him?
How do you help the new neighbour settle in?
Who do you ask for advice on the organisation?
How do you respect the wishes of the new person?
What do you do if he previously lived in a single-family house?

q.en: Hi, Mark! <g>Have</g> you already <g>heard</g>? A new neighbour has moved into our apartment building. Shall we plan together how we welcome him?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: I heard he used to live in a single-family house and now lives in an apartment building for the first time – by the way, he's an architect. We could invite the new architect to our little building party right away.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the other neighbours.
We could also let the student on the third floor know, he'll probably be happy to help set up.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also ask the police officer next door, he probably already knows a few nice stories from the neighbourhood.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also let the new intern on the ground floor know? He doesn't know anyone here yet.
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether we have enough space for everyone.
One idea would be that we also invite the journalist from the second floor, maybe he'll even write a nice article about our building.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the new neighbour even likes so many strangers.
Maybe it would be best if we ask our caretaker first – we can definitely trust the expert for this kind of party.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also let the nice customer from the bakery on the corner know, he knows almost everyone in the neighbourhood.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we simply respect the opinion of the new person at the start, and let him settle in peacefully first.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we invite the architect, the police officer and the journalist, let the student and the intern know, get tips from the expert, our caretaker, and also let the customer from the bakery know. And of course we'll respect the opinion of the new person, in case he'd rather have some peace and quiet at first. I'm already looking forward to our building party! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: Anna and Nina want to rent a flat together that they've been interested in for a long time.
Task: Plan the next steps together with your flatmate.
These points will help you:
When do you talk to the landlord?
How much money do you need for the deposit?
What's in the rental contract?
Who takes care of the renovation?
What notice period applies?

q.en: Hi, Nina! I found the flat <g>I've been interested in</g> for a long time. Shall we plan together how we proceed now?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: First we should call the landlord we spoke to on the phone again and arrange a viewing.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the deposit.
We could already start setting aside money for the deposit we need to save for.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we carefully read through the rental contract, in which all the important rules are written – especially whether it's about the cold rent or the warm rent.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we take another look at the balcony you can supposedly see the whole park from?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify who takes care of the renovation.
One idea would be that we first clarify who pays for the renovation the previous tenants are probably still responsible for.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the cold rent will really stay as cheap as promised.
Maybe it would be best if we also ask the real estate agent we contacted again.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also already think about who the next tenant we'd hand the flat over to could be, in case we ever move out.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also carefully read up on the notice period after which we could move out again at the earliest, at the end.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we call the landlord, save up for the deposit, carefully read through the rental contract, take another look at the balcony, clarify the renovation, ask the real estate agent about the cold rent, already think about a possible next tenant, and carefully read up on the notice period. I'm already looking forward to our new flat! Thanks for the idea, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend want to find a place together where you feel good.
Task: Plan together with your friend how you'll find this place.
These points will help you:
Which neighbourhood do you want to live in?
How high can the utility costs be?
What do you write in your wanted ad?
Where is your favourite spot?
What matters most to you?

q.en: Hi, Julia! I'm looking for a place where I really feel good. Shall we think together about how to find that?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We could first choose a neighbourhood where a lot of young people live.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the utility costs.
We could write down exactly everything that we spend each month, so we know what we can afford.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also look for a flat with a garden where we can sit in the summer.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we write a wanted ad together, in which we mention something that really matters to us?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how big the café we're looking for should be.
One idea would be that we look for a café nearby where we can meet regularly.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can really plan everything in advance.
Maybe it would be best if we first make sure that nothing that bothers us is in the new flat.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also look for a favourite spot in the neighbourhood where we both feel good.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we decide together at the end what the best thing that we've found is for us.
Are you okay with that, Julia?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we look for a neighbourhood with lots of young people, write down everything we spend, look for a flat with a garden, write a wanted ad with what matters to us, find a café nearby, make sure nothing bothers us, look for a shared favourite spot, and decide at the end what's best for us. I'm already looking forward to our search! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend have found a house you like and want to present it.
Task: Plan together with your friend how you'll present the house.
These points will help you:
Which family would like the house?
Who do you show the house to first?
Who else do you still need to inform?
Who do you ask for advice or help?
What do you tell people about the outskirts and the suburb?

q.en: Hi, David! I've <g>finally found</g> the house I really like! Shall we plan together how to present it best?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We could first think about the family who would like the house most – so a family with children.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the outskirts of the city.
We could also already invite the married couple who we want to show the house to first.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also talk to the current tenants who we still need to inform.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we give the tradesperson who we already trust the last repairs to do?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether the property management already knows.
One idea would be that we get information from the property management who we can ask all our questions.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the owner agrees with everything.
Maybe it would be best if we ask the owner who the property belongs to a few more questions.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also think about the children who would surely like the big garden.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also explain the quiet suburb on the outskirts right away to the first guest who we show the house to.
Are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we think about the family, invite the married couple, talk to the tenants, give the tradesperson the last repairs, get information from the property management, ask the owner, think about the children with the garden, and explain the suburb on the outskirts to the first guest. I'm already looking forward to presenting the house! Thanks for the idea, Anna!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend have found a flat listing with lots of exaggerated adjectives.
Task: Plan together how you'll check whether the flat is really that good.
These points will help you:
How do you check the location and the view?
How do you test whether the flat is really quiet and bright?
How high is the demand for a flat like this?
Does the price really stay that cheap?
How modern are the fittings really?

q.en: Hi, Alex! I <g>found</g> a flat listing that sounds really exaggerated. Shall we check together whether it's actually true?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: The listing says the flat is super affordable – but I'd want to take a closer look at that before we believe it.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the location.
We could also check whether the flat is really as highly insulated as the listing says.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we listen carefully during the viewing to check whether the street is really as extremely quiet as promised.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also take a look at the view and check whether the rooms are really as extra bright as the listing says?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how high the demand for a flat like this really is.
One idea would be that we imagine whether the kitchen is really super bright, or whether that's just an advertising trick.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the price will really stay that cheap in the end.
Maybe it would be best if we also check the fittings, because the listing says the kitchen is ultra-modern.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also make sure the flat isn't overpriced in the end, just because the demand is so high.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also convince ourselves at the end whether the neighbourhood is really as extra quiet as described in the listing.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we check whether the flat is really super affordable, highly insulated, extremely quiet and extra bright, check the ultra-modern fittings, make sure it isn't overpriced, and convince ourselves whether the neighbourhood is extra quiet too. Then we can finally imagine what our new home really looks like! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: David and Nina want to call the property management about a flat.
Task: Prepare the formal phone call together with your conversation partner.
These points will help you:
How do you politely answer/identify yourself on the phone?
What do you ask about the flat (living space, location, neighbourhood)?
What do you do if you're connected to the wrong person?
What do you say if no one picks up?
How do you politely say goodbye?

q.en: Hi, Nina! We should call the property management about the flat. Shall we think together about what to say?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: If someone picks up, we should first politely identify ourselves and give our names.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the extension number.
We could ask right away for the correct extension for the rental department, in case we're connected to the wrong person.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we politely ask whether they can transfer us, in case the wrong person picks up.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also ask about the exact living space, so we know whether the flat is really that big?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether we should also ask about neighbourhood help.
One idea would be that we also ask whether there's neighbourhood help in the building, that would matter to us.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the area is really as child-friendly as the listing says.
Maybe it would be best if we also ask whether the neighbourhood is really child-friendly and lively.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also ask how far it is to the city centre, that matters to both of us.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we leave a short message on the answering machine if no one picks up, and say goodbye politely.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we politely identify ourselves, ask for the extension, get transferred if needed, ask about the living space, the neighbourhood help, whether the area is child-friendly and lively, and how far it is to the city centre. If no one picks up, we leave a message on the answering machine and say a friendly goodbye. I'm already looking forward to the call! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend wants to submit a naturalisation application, and you want to help him prepare.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll support him.
These points will help you:
What documents does he need for the passport?
How much patience and work is ahead of him?
How can you give him hope for the future?
What motivates him to make the effort?
Where can he get examples of successful applications?

q.en: Hi, Anna! Our friend wants to submit a naturalisation application. Shall we think together about how we can help him?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: A German passport means a lot to him, so we should first help him gather all the necessary documents.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about his time.
We could also keep in mind: hard work alone often isn't enough, he also needs our support with learning German.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we tell him: great patience is important in this process, it often takes longer than expected.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we tell him that great success awaits him in the end, if he keeps going?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether he even already knows how the application exactly works.
One idea would be that we show him what a new life with a German passport could look like for him.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we're putting too much pressure on him.
Maybe it would be best if we simply tell him that new hope can already give him strength now.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also emphasise that a secure future for his family is the real goal.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we show him, using honest naturalisation applications from other people, how it's best done.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we help him with the documents for the German passport, support him with the hard work, remind him about great patience, tell him about the great success at the end, show him his new life, give him new hope, emphasise the secure future for his family, and show him honest naturalisation applications from other people. All the effort will be worth it in the end! Thanks for the idea, Mark!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend is getting German citizenship, and you want to prepare the naturalisation ceremony together.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll accompany him.
These points will help you:
What awaits him at the ceremony?
Which conditions did he have to meet?
What problems did he have along the way?
Who helped him at the authority?
What do you say to him about his new fundamental right?

q.en: Hi, Alex! Our friend is finally getting German citizenship! Shall we plan together how we prepare the naturalisation ceremony for him?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: There will surely be a lot of laughing children at the ceremony too, that makes the atmosphere even nicer.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the fundamental rights.
We could also keep in mind that there will surely be a waiting crowd of other people who are also getting their citizenship.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also tell him that the rising number of naturalisations shows how many people want to stay here.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we explain the existing conditions for naturalisation to him once more, so that he understands everything?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether there's still a growing problem with appointments at the authority.
One idea would be that we tell him that the growing problem with waiting times at the authority is supposed to get better soon.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether a helpful staff member was really able to help him.
Maybe it would be best if we ask him whether a helpful staff member at the office has already explained everything to him.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also suggest a convincing explanation for his speech, of why Germany has become so important to him.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we tell him that the sometimes stressful situation with the authorities is now finally over.
Are you okay with that, Alex?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we look forward to the laughing children at the ceremony, tell him about the waiting crowd and the rising number of naturalisations, explain the existing conditions to him, talk about the growing problem with waiting times, ask about a helpful staff member, suggest a convincing explanation for his speech, and tell him that the stressful situation is now over. His German citizenship is a real fundamental right he can be proud of! Thanks for the idea, Julia!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend finally has to finish his naturalisation application, and you want to help him with the final check.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner what else you'll check.
These points will help you:
Are all the documents completely filled out?
Has he already passed the exam and completed the integration course?
Are there any open deadlines or inquiries?
When is his next appointment?
Are all the certificates notarised?

q.en: Hi, Anna! Our friend finally has to finish his naturalisation application. Shall we go through everything together once more?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We could first check whether every filled-out document is really complete.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the dual citizenship.
We could also check whether he has already submitted proof of the passed exam.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also check that no missed deadline is delaying the whole thing.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also check whether every answered inquiry from the authority is properly saved?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether freedom of religion even comes up in the constitution test.
One idea would be that we keep a copy of the submitted application for himself.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we've already planned the integration course correctly.
Maybe it would be best if we also confirm the arranged appointment at the office once more, so that nothing goes wrong.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also find the certificate for the completed integration course again.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also check at the end whether every certified document is really included.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we check every filled-out document, the passed exam and the missed deadline, look at every answered inquiry, keep a copy of the submitted application, confirm the arranged appointment, find the certificate for the completed integration course, and check every certified document. Then nothing will stand in the way of his dual citizenship! Thanks for the idea, Julia!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend has to go to the office to renew his papers, and he doesn't know exactly what to bring.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner what alternatives there are.
These points will help you:
Does he need the passport, or is the ID card enough?
Does he register his residence online, or does he go in person?
Does he need a witness?
Does the office accept a copy?
Does he get an appointment today or only tomorrow?

q.en: Hi, Anna! Our friend has to go to the office to renew his papers, but he doesn't know exactly what he needs to bring. Shall we go through the options together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: Either he brings his passport, or he just shows his ID card, either should be enough.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the residence.
We could tell him: either he registers his residence online, or he goes to the office in person.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we tell him: either he renews his right of residence right now, or he waits another month and risks a long waiting list.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we tell him, either he brings the registration certificate along, or he gets it right there on site?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify whether he even needs a witness.
One idea would be that we explain to him: either he brings a witness along, or he goes alone, that depends on the office.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether the office even accepts copies.
Maybe it would be best if we ask beforehand: either the office accepts a copy, or we definitely need the original.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also clarify whether he gets an appointment either today or only tomorrow.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also tell him to prepare for the test, because either a question about democracy comes up, or he simply gets lucky.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we'll tell him: either passport or ID card, either online or in person, either renew now or wait, either bring the registration certificate or get it on site, either with a witness or alone, either copy or original, either an appointment today or tomorrow, and either a question about democracy or luck at the exam. Then he'll be perfectly prepared! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: Your friend has to fill out and submit the naturalisation application completely.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner how you'll support him with this.
These points will help you:
What does he need to prove?
Is his residence permit still valid?
How high is the fee?
How does he prepare for the interview with the caseworker?
Why is it important to contribute to society?

q.en: Hi, Mark! Our friend finally has to fill out the naturalisation application completely. Shall we think together about how we can help him with that?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We should first check whether the application is really complete and whether he can prove his German language skills well enough.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the fundamental values that are asked about in the application.
We could go through the most important questions about that together with him.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also check whether his residence permit is still valid for long enough.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also help him with the fee, so he knows exactly how much he needs to pay?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify how he can best deal with all the bureaucracy.
One idea would be that we make him a list with all the steps, so he doesn't forget anything.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether he has already prepared enough for the interview.
Maybe it would be best if we practise a few typical questions with him.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also think about which questions the caseworker might ask him.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also tell him how important it is that he contributes to society.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we check whether the application is complete and the German skills are proven, go through the fundamental values, check the residence permit, help with the fee, make a list against the bureaucracy, practise questions for the interview with the caseworker, and remind him how important his contribution to society is. Then nothing should be able to go wrong anymore! Thanks for the idea, David!

task.en:
Situation: After the stressful naturalisation process, you and your friend want to celebrate and then travel together.
Task: Plan the party and the trip together with your conversation partner.
These points will help you:
How do you celebrate so that you can recover?
Who do you invite to the party?
When do you depart?
What are you looking forward to the most?
What do you hope for during your time together?

q.en: Hi, David! After all the stress with the naturalisation application, we've really earned a celebration. Shall we plan together how we celebrate and then travel afterwards?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We should organise a big party, because we really worked hard for this.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the budget.
We could have a simple party, but still invite enough guests.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we invite all our friends, so we should make a list right away.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we hold the party on a weekday? Many people are tired from everyday life, but they'll still come gladly.
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify when we should best depart.
One idea would be that we plan the trip only a week after the party, because we want to properly recover afterwards.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we can already say for sure that we have enough time.
Maybe it would be best if we first check that we really have enough vacation days for the trip.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's already book the trip once we're both sure.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we already look forward to the trip now, even though we're still a bit exhausted from the application.
Are you okay with that, David?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we organise a party, invite all our friends, plan the trip a week later, check our vacation days, book the trip, and already look forward to it now. I hope we can really recover well afterwards, before we have to depart again for work! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend are planning the final details before your trip together.
Task: Plan together what you still need to take care of before departure.
These points will help you:
Who is coming along later?
What are you sending back?
Where are you driving on to?
What are you bringing for friends?
When are you coming back, and who is picking you up?

q.en: Hi, Anna! <g>Before</g> we go on our trip, we still need to clarify a few things. Shall we plan the final steps together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: Julia unfortunately can only join us two days later, we should plan for that already.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the suitcases.
We could say: we'll just send back the things we don't need beforehand.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we do it like this: before departure we'll throw away the old things in the fridge.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we decide this: after the first overnight stay we'll drive on right away.
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify what we should bring for our friends.
One idea would be that we do this: we'll bring everyone a small present.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we already know exactly when we're coming back.
Maybe it would be best if we settle this right away: we'll come back on Sunday evening.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also clarify: do we pick someone up from the station, or do we take a taxi?
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also take care of this: before departure we'll quickly tidy up the flat.
Are you okay with that, Anna?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, Julia will join us two days later, we'll send back things we don't need, throw away the old things, drive on after the first overnight stay, bring everyone a present, come back on Sunday evening, either pick someone up from the station or take a taxi, and quickly tidy up the flat beforehand. I'm already looking forward to our trip! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend witnessed someone breaking into the neighbouring flat.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner what you'll do now.
These points will help you:
When do you report the break-in?
What was stolen?
How do you describe the suspect?
What do you testify to the police?
What evidence do you have?

q.en: Hi, Mark! I think I just <g>saw</g> someone <g>break</g> into the neighbouring flat! Shall we think together about what we do now?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We should report the break-in to the police right away, so they can come as quickly as possible.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the stolen items.
We could first check whether we can see what exactly was stolen.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we definitely don't enter the crime scene before the police arrive, otherwise we might destroy evidence.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we also describe to the police exactly where we last saw the suspect, so they can apprehend him faster?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify what exactly we should testify.
One idea would be that we think in advance about what exactly we want to testify to the police, so that we don't forget anything.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we even have enough evidence.
Maybe it would be best if we also take a photo of the door, that could be important as evidence later.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also expect that we'll officially be summoned to testify later.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we simply hope that the police can arrest the burglar quickly.
Are you okay with that, Mark?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we report the break-in to the police, check what was stolen, don't enter the crime scene, describe the suspect exactly, think about our testimony, take a photo as evidence, expect to be summoned, and hope the police arrest the burglar soon. I really hope everything turns out well! Thanks for the idea, Nina!

task.en:
Situation: You and your friend are in a new city with a whole day to spend.
Task: Plan together with your conversation partner what you'll see.
These points will help you:
Which landmark do you visit first?
How do you get there by tram?
How do you ensure your safety?
What do you do in bad weather?
What verdict do you reach about the city in the end?

q.en: Hi, Nina! We're in this new city now and still have a whole day. Shall we plan together what we look at?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
I have a suggestion: We could walk from the youth hostel to the city's biggest landmark.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the fact that this is a foreign city.
We could take a bit of care for our own safety and not be out alone too late in the evening.
How do you find that?

a1.en:
Perfect, that's what we'll do.
My suggestion would be that we also visit the famous monument in the old town, it's supposed to be really impressive.
Do you agree with that?

q2.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
How about we board the tram and transfer once, so we get there faster?
Does that work for you?

a2.en:
That's okay with me, however we'd still need to clarify at which stop we need to get off.
One idea would be that we note down the correct stop to get off at beforehand.
What do you think of that?

q3.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure whether we have enough time for all the architecture of the old town.
Maybe it would be best if we just focus on the most beautiful architecture, instead of trying to see everything.
What do you think about that?

a3.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's also make a plan B: if it rains, we'll simply flee into a museum.
How do you see it?

q4.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we reach a verdict together at the end of the day about which city we've liked best so far.
Are you okay with that, Nina?

a4.en: Yes, of course! So, we walk from the youth hostel to the landmark, take care of our own safety, visit the monument in the old town, board the tram and transfer once, remember the right stop to get off at, focus on the most beautiful architecture, flee to a museum if it rains, and reach a verdict at the end about our favourite place. I'm already looking forward to the day! Thanks for the idea, Alex!

sentence.en: Could you please help me carry the box?

explanation.en:
„Könnten“ (subjunctive II) sounds more polite than the simple „Können“.
„Müssen“ would express an obligation, not a polite request.

sentence.en: Would you be so kind as to pass me the salt?

explanation.en:
The fixed, very polite phrase is „Wären Sie so freundlich …?“ (subjunctive II of „sein“).
„Sind“ would be the simple present tense, less polite.

sentence.en: I would have a request, if you have a moment.

explanation.en:
„wenn“ here introduces a polite, indirect condition.
„ob“ would express uncertainty, not a condition.

sentence.en: Don't forget to read the house rules.

explanation.en:
After „vergessen, etwas zu tun“ (to forget to do something) you need the infinitive with „zu“.
„lesen“ without „zu“ would be grammatically wrong in this position.

sentence.en: It's no fun to go shopping every day.

explanation.en:
With separable verbs like „einkaufen“, „zu“ goes between the prefix and the verb: „einzukaufen“.
„kaufen“ alone would be the wrong, non-separable verb.

sentence.en: She has no time to visit us today.

explanation.en:
After „Zeit haben, etwas zu tun“ (to have time to do something), the infinitive with „zu“ comes at the end.
„besucht“ would be a conjugated form, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: He speaks both German and English fluently.

explanation.en:
„sowohl … als auch“ (both … and) connects two positive, equal things.
„weder“ would introduce a double negation, but the statement here is positive.

sentence.en: I have neither time nor desire to go out today.

explanation.en:
„weder … noch“ (neither … nor) negates two things at the same time.
„sowohl“ would connect two positive things, but here both are negated.

sentence.en: The shop is open neither on Saturday nor on Sunday.

explanation.en:
„weder … noch“ fits because both days are excluded (the shop is not open on either day).
„sowohl“ would express the opposite.

sentence.en: During the quiet hours, you may not listen to loud music.

explanation.en:
„darf … nicht/kein-“ expresses a prohibition (a house rule).
„muss“ would express an obligation, not a prohibition.

sentence.en: Every tenant must sign the house rules.

explanation.en:
„muss“ expresses an obligation that applies to all tenants.
„darf“ would only express permission, not an obligation.

sentence.en: Can I help you carry the suitcase for a moment?

explanation.en:
„kann“ here politely offers an ability/help.
„muss“ would express an obligation, not an offer.

sentence.en: We moved into the new flat last week.

explanation.en:
For direction (where to?), the two-way preposition „in“ is used with accusative: „in die Wohnung“.
„an“ would not fit with „ziehen in etwas“ (to move into something).

sentence.en: The stroller is standing in the stairwell.

explanation.en:
For position (where?), the two-way preposition „in“ is used with dative: „in dem Treppenhaus“.
„zu“ would only express a direction.

sentence.en: Please don't put the box on the escape route.

explanation.en:
For an action with direction (where to put something?), the two-way preposition „auf“ is used with accusative.
„an“ would describe a different position, not „on a surface“.

sentence.en: I have to hurry, otherwise I'll be late.

explanation.en:
„sich beeilen“ (to hurry) is a reflexive verb with accusative: 1st person singular = „mich“.
„mir“ would be the dative, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: Why are you getting annoyed with the neighbours again?

explanation.en:
„sich ärgern“ (to get annoyed) needs the reflexive pronoun in the accusative: 2nd person singular = „dich“.
„dir“ would be the dative, which is grammatically wrong here.

sentence.en: The children are very happy about the holidays.

explanation.en:
„sich freuen“ (to be happy) needs the reflexive pronoun in the accusative: 3rd person plural = „sich“.
„ihnen“ would be the dative plural, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: That was not a mistake, but a deliberate decision.

explanation.en:
„sondern“ (but rather) follows a negation to express a contrast.
„aber“ would stand without a preceding negation and doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: The man who lives next to me is very friendly.

explanation.en:
The relative pronoun is the subject of the clause (he lives), so it is in the nominative: „der“.
„den“ would be the accusative, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: That's not my complaint, but my colleague's.

explanation.en:
„sondern“ corrects a previous negation with the correct alternative.
„aber“ would not express a real contrast to the negation here.

sentence.en: The invoice that I received last week was wrong.

explanation.en:
The relative pronoun is the accusative object (I received the invoice), feminine singular accusative = „die“.
„der“ would be dative or nominative, grammatically wrong here.

sentence.en: The dress that I would like to exchange is too small.

explanation.en:
The neuter singular accusative relative pronoun is „das“ (same form as nominative for neuter).
„den“ would be masculine accusative and doesn't fit „das Kleid“.

sentence.en: The neighbours whom we invited to the party are coming at eight.

explanation.en:
The plural accusative relative pronoun is „die“ (same for all genders in the plural).
„denen“ would be the dative plural, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: He didn't answer the phone, he might still be at work.

explanation.en:
„dürfte“ (subjunctive II of „dürfen“) expresses a cautious assumption.
„muss“ would be a much more certain statement, almost a fact.

sentence.en: The account should already be opened, he's already received the card.

explanation.en:
„müsste“ (subjunctive II of „müssen“) expresses a logical, fairly certain assumption.
„soll“ would express an order or a rumour, not one's own assumption.

sentence.en: In this weather, it could be very crowded at the organic farm today.

explanation.en:
„könnte“ (subjunctive II of „können“) expresses an uncertain possibility.
„muss“ would be far too certain a statement for a mere assumption.

sentence.en: Our neighbour's car is parked in front of our door again.

explanation.en:
The masculine singular genitive of the definite article is „des“, the noun gets „-n“: „des Nachbarn“.
„dem“ would be the dative, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: The costs of the insurance have risen this year.

explanation.en:
The feminine singular genitive of the definite article is „der“ (same form as feminine dative).
„die“ would be the nominative or accusative, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: Because of the theft, he had to have the card blocked.

explanation.en:
The preposition „wegen“ (because of) requires the genitive: „wegen des Diebstahls“.
„dem“ would be the dative, which is less common with „wegen“ in standard language.

sentence.en: He cancelled the insurance although it was very cheap.

explanation.en:
„obwohl“ (although) expresses a contrast (cancelling although it was cheap).
„weil“ would give a reason, which doesn't make sense here.

sentence.en: Although it was very cold outside, we went for a walk.

explanation.en:
„Obwohl“ (although) introduces a clause of contrast (going for a walk despite the cold).
„Weil“ would give a reason for the walk, which would be illogical here.

sentence.en: She passed the exam although she barely had time to study.

explanation.en:
„obwohl“ describes an unexpected contrast (passing despite little study time).
„damit“ would express a purpose, which doesn't make sense here.

sentence.en: The transfer hasn't arrived, that's why I'm calling the bank.

explanation.en:
„deshalb“ (that's why) states the consequence of an event.
„obwohl“ would express a contrast, not a consequence.

sentence.en: The damage was small; nevertheless, she had to inform the insurance.

explanation.en:
„trotzdem“ (nevertheless) expresses an unexpected contrast (informing despite the damage being small).
„deshalb“ would express a logical consequence, not a contrast.

sentence.en: I sent the damage report immediately so that the insurance can react quickly.

explanation.en:
„damit“ (so that) states the purpose of sending it immediately.
„trotzdem“ would express a contrast, not a purpose.

sentence.en: In the past, I only ate fast food, today I cook myself.

explanation.en:
With „früher“ (in the past), you need the simple past in written/narrative texts: „ernährte“.
„ernähre“ would be present tense and doesn't fit with „früher“.

sentence.en: His diet consisted almost only of bread and sausage in the past.

explanation.en:
„bestand“ is the simple past of „bestehen aus“ (to consist of) and fits with „früher“.
„besteht“ would be present tense and would not fit the past.

sentence.en: As children, we often lived with our grandparents.

explanation.en:
With „als Kinder“ (looking back), you use the simple past: „wohnten“.
„wohnen“ would be present tense, which doesn't fit the time frame here.

sentence.en: The vending machine was broken, that's why I couldn't buy coffee.

explanation.en:
„deshalb“ states the logical consequence (broken → no coffee).
„trotzdem“ would express a contrast, not a consequence.

sentence.en: He doesn't eat regularly; nevertheless, he is very healthy.

explanation.en:
„trotzdem“ expresses an unexpected contrast.
„deswegen“ would express a logical consequence, which doesn't make sense here.

sentence.en: We have changed our eating habits, that's why we feel fitter.

explanation.en:
„deswegen“ (like „deshalb“) states the consequence of a change.
„trotzdem“ would express an unsuitable contrast here.

sentence.en: The results of the survey were surprising.

explanation.en:
In spoken language, the genitive is often replaced by „von“ + dative: „von der Umfrage“.
„der“ alone (without „von“) would be the classic genitive here.

sentence.en: The price of the snack was much too high.

explanation.en:
„von“ + dative is the spoken alternative to the genitive: „von dem Snack“ (= „des Snacks“).
„des“ would be the classic genitive; here the alternative is being tested.

sentence.en: The size of the portion was much too big for me.

explanation.en:
„von“ + dative replaces the genitive here in everyday language: „von der Portion“.
„die“ would be nominative/accusative and doesn't fit grammatically here.

sentence.en: Since I have been living in Germany, I eat much healthier.

explanation.en:
„Seit(dem)“ (since) introduces a point in the past that continues until now.
„Bis“ (until) would express an end point in the future, not a starting point in the past.

sentence.en: Many things have surprised me since I have been working here.

explanation.en:
„seitdem“ describes an ongoing period from a starting point in the past.
„damit“ would express a purpose, not a time reference.

sentence.en: I see the cultural differences much more clearly since I have been living here.

explanation.en:
„seit“ marks the beginning of a situation that continues until now.
„weil“ would give a reason, not a point in time.

sentence.en: Who are you waiting for here? — For my brother.

explanation.en:
For questions about people, you use „preposition + wen/wem“: „Auf wen“.
„Worauf“ would ask about a thing, not a person.

sentence.en: What are you waiting for here? — For the bus.

explanation.en:
For questions about things, you use the pronominal adverb „wo(r) + preposition“: „Worauf“.
„Auf wen“ would ask about a person, but here it's about a bus.

sentence.en: Who do you actually speak your native language with?

explanation.en:
After a preposition + question about a person in the dative, „wem“ is used: „Mit wem“.
„was“ would ask about a thing, not a person.

sentence.en: I waited until I had enough experience for the job.

explanation.en:
„bis“ (until) marks the end point of a waiting period.
„seit“ would express a starting point in the past, not an end.

sentence.en: Nobody noticed the mistake until the boss read the list again.

explanation.en:
„bis“ shows the point at which the situation changes (the mistake gets noticed).
„damit“ would express a purpose, not a point in time.

sentence.en: We'll stay here until the rain stops.

explanation.en:
„bis“ states the point at which an action ends.
„wenn“ would express a repeated or general condition, but the clear end point „bis“ fits better here.

sentence.en: What were you most annoyed about in the course?

explanation.en:
For a question about a thing with „sich ärgern über“, the pronominal adverb „worüber“ is used.
„Über wen“ would ask about a person, but here it's about a thing/situation.

sentence.en: The topic is a taboo for us; we almost never talk about it.

explanation.en:
„darüber“ (pronominal adverb) replaces „über das Thema“ (about the topic).
„damit“ would express a means or tool, not the topic of conversation.

sentence.en: There was a misunderstanding, but we have already talked about it.

explanation.en:
„darüber“ replaces „über das Missverständnis“ and refers to something already mentioned.
„dabei“ would express a simultaneous action, not a topic of conversation.

sentence.en: The examination will take place tomorrow morning.

explanation.en:
The future tense (Futur I) is formed with „werden“ + infinitive: „wird … stattfinden“.
„ist“ would be present tense and doesn't express a clear statement about the future.

sentence.en: The patient will be transferred to another ward tomorrow.

explanation.en:
Here „wird“ is part of the future passive: „wird … verlegt“ (future passive).
„hat“ would introduce a different tense (perfect), which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: Next week we will take out a new insurance policy.

explanation.en:
Future I: „werden“ + infinitive („abschließen“) expresses a planned future action.
„haben“ would introduce a perfect tense, not the future.

sentence.en: In an emergency, you must not only stay calm but also call 112 quickly.

explanation.en:
„nicht nur … sondern auch“ (not only … but also) connects two important, positive actions.
„weder“ would negate both actions, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: During the fall, he not only hurt his arm but also his head.

explanation.en:
After „nicht nur“, „sondern auch“ always follows, never „aber“.
„aber“ would express a simple contrast, not the fixed paired structure.

sentence.en: In the accident, not only the drivers but also two pedestrians were injured.

explanation.en:
The fixed construction is „nicht nur …, sondern auch …“.
„und“ would only express a simple list, without special emphasis.

sentence.en: She filled in the form carefully in order not to make any mistakes.

explanation.en:
„um … zu“ is used when the subject of the main and subordinate clause is the same (she fills in, she makes no mistakes).
„damit“ would be used if the subjects were different.

sentence.en: He needed the bandage in order to protect the wound.

explanation.en:
„um … zu“ expresses the purpose of an action when the subject stays the same.
„weil“ would give a reason, not a purpose.

sentence.en: We saved energy in order to protect the environment.

explanation.en:
„um … zu“ fits because the subject (we) is the same in both parts of the sentence.
„damit“ would be needed if a different subject fulfilled the purpose.

sentence.en: The doctor explained the prognosis precisely so that the family understands everything.

explanation.en:
„damit“ fits because the subject of the subordinate clause (the family) is different from the subject of the main clause (the doctor).
„um … zu“ would only work with the same subject.

sentence.en: The doctor has to operate on him today so that his condition doesn't get worse.

explanation.en:
„damit“ states the goal of the operation from the perspective of a different subject (the condition).
„weil“ would give a reason, not a goal.

sentence.en: She sends the damage report immediately so that the insurance can react quickly.

explanation.en:
„damit“ fits because the subject in the subordinate clause (the insurance) is different from the main clause (she).
„dass“ would only state a fact, not a goal.

sentence.en: In Germany, waste is sorted very precisely.

explanation.en:
The present passive is formed with „werden“ + past participle: „wird … getrennt“.
„ist“ would describe more of a state (stative passive), not the process.

sentence.en: The energy consumption in our house is now precisely monitored.

explanation.en:
„wird … kontrolliert“ is present passive and describes an ongoing process.
„hat“ would be a perfect auxiliary verb, which doesn't fit here.

sentence.en: Old bottles are processed into new glass.

explanation.en:
With plural subjects, „werden“ is used (not „wird“): „Flaschen werden verarbeitet“.
„sind“ would describe an already completed state (stative passive), not the process.

sentence.en: This year, we have avoided a lot of plastic waste.

explanation.en:
„vermeiden“ forms the perfect tense with „haben“: „haben … vermieden“.
„sind“ is only used with verbs of motion or change of state.

sentence.en: We have sold our car and switched to a bicycle.

explanation.en:
„verkaufen“ needs „haben“ in the perfect, while „umsteigen“ (motion/change) needs „sind“.
„sind“ would be wrong here for „verkaufen“.

sentence.en: Have you already saved energy this year? — Yes, we have replaced our lamps.

explanation.en:
„austauschen“ forms the perfect with „haben“ (transitive verb with accusative object).
„sind“ would only be used with intransitive verbs of motion.

sentence.en: I am already really looking forward to the festival next week.

explanation.en:
„sich freuen auf“ (+accusative) is used for something that is still to come (future).
„über“ would be used for something that has already happened.

sentence.en: Despite the uncertain weather, many people wanted to take part in the tour.

explanation.en:
„teilnehmen an“ (+dative) is a fixed verb-preposition combination.
„bei“ doesn't fit with this fixed verb here.

sentence.en: The neighbours often exchange views about unknown artists.

explanation.en:
„sich austauschen über“ (+accusative) is a fixed verb-preposition combination for conversation topics.
„von“ doesn't fit grammatically with „austauschen“ here.

sentence.en: What is the new exhibition at the museum about?

explanation.en:
„handeln von“ (to be about) is a fixed combination, so you ask with „wovon“.
„worüber“ would fit a different verb, e.g. „sprechen über“.

sentence.en: What exactly does the library's new offer refer to?

explanation.en:
„sich beziehen auf“ (to refer to) needs the pronominal adverb „worauf“ in the question.
„wovon“ would fit a different verb, but not here.

sentence.en: What were you most enthusiastic about at the festival?

explanation.en:
„begeistert sein von“ (to be enthusiastic about) is a fixed combination, hence „wovon“.
„woran“ would fit a different verb, e.g. „denken an“.

sentence.en: So, how long does the tour actually take?

explanation.en:
„denn“ in questions shows genuine, friendly interest.
„doch“ fits better with statements or requests, not this type of question.

sentence.en: So, how much does admission for the tour actually cost?

explanation.en:
„eigentlich“ in a question shows casual, genuine interest.
„schon“ would rather express impatience or a different meaning.

sentence.en: So, how was the library tour?

explanation.en:
„denn“ makes the question friendlier and shows genuine interest in the conversation.
„ja“ as a modal particle is mostly used in statements, not in wh-questions.

task.en:
You live in an apartment building. For a few weeks now, there has been very loud music and arguing in the stairwell in the evenings. You are writing to the property management.

1. Reason for your letter
2. Since when and how often the noise occurs
3. What consequences the noise has for you
4. What you expect from the property management

parts.en: Leipzig, 15 January 2025
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> there is very loud music and arguing in the stairwell of our apartment building in the evenings.
Ever since a new neighbor moved in on the third floor, I have heard loud music from the stairwell <r>almost every evening</r>.
<r>This means for me that</r> I can no longer relax in the evenings and have often slept badly because of it.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> speak with the neighbor. It would also be very kind of you to remind him of the house rules.
<r>I hope to hear back from you soon.</r>
Best regards,
Julia Neumann

task.en:
You want to get to know the neighbors in your building better and are organizing a small neighborhood party in the courtyard. Write an email to the neighbors.

1. Reason for your email
2. When and where the party takes place
3. What everyone can bring
4. A request to let you know who is coming

parts.en: Subject: Small party in the courtyard on Saturday
Dear neighbors,
<r>I would like to warmly invite you all to a small party</r> so that we as neighbors in the building can finally get to know each other better and celebrate together in the courtyard.
<r>The party will take place on Saturday, 20 September, at 3 p.m.</r> If it rains, we will celebrate in the community room instead.
<r>I would be very grateful if</r> everyone could bring something to eat or drink, so that we have a small buffet together.
<r>I would be very happy if</r> you could let me know by Friday whether you're coming.
<r>I'm already looking forward to a nice afternoon with you all.</r>
Best,
Mark Fischer

task.en:
You are going on a two-week holiday and want to ask your neighbor for a favor. Write her a letter.

1. Reason for your letter
2. What you are asking her to do
3. Where the key is and what needs to be done
4. How you would like to thank her

parts.en: Hamburg, 3 July 2025
Dear Sabine,
<r>I have a favor to ask you</r>: I'm leaving for a two-week holiday tomorrow, and could you possibly help me?
<r>Could you please</r> water the flowers twice a week? Also, could you pick up the mail briefly, too?
You'll find the spare key in the mailbox. While I'm on holiday, you don't need to worry about anything else.
<r>As a thank you, I'll bring you</r> a small gift from my holiday, so that you know how grateful I am.
<r>I'll be in touch as soon as I'm back.</r>
Take care,
Anna Vogel

topic.en: A cleaning schedule for the stairwell

task.en:
In your apartment building, no one has been cleaning the stairwell regularly so far. You propose a shared cleaning schedule to the tenants. Write an email to all tenants.

1. Reason for your email
2. Why a cleaning schedule makes sense
3. What the plan should look like
4. A request for feedback

parts.en: Subject: Proposal for a cleaning schedule in the stairwell
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I would like to let you know that</r> it is difficult to keep the stairwell in our building clean regularly, because so far no one really takes care of it.
<r>I therefore suggest</r> making a fixed schedule in order to save the cost of a cleaning company and share the responsibility fairly.
<r>I imagine that</r> each family takes on a week, which we determine together, and then passes it on to the next family.
<r>I would be very grateful if</r> you could share your opinion with me briefly. That's why I am asking you to reply by the end of the month.
<r>I look forward to your reply.</r>
Best regards,
David Berger

task.en:
You recently moved into a new apartment building and have some questions about the house rules. You are writing to the property management.

1. Reason for your letter
2. What you would like to know about the quiet hours
3. What you would like to know about waste separation and parking
4. A request for a written reply

parts.en: Munich, 12 February 2025
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> I recently moved into your building and still have a few questions about the house rules that I would like to clarify.
<r>I would like to ask you</r> exactly what I need to follow regarding the quiet hours, because unfortunately the house rules don't say anything specific about that.
<r>I would also like to know</r> whether there are fixed rules that I need to follow regarding waste separation and parking.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> send me the complete house rules in writing. I would also be glad to have all the rules at a glance then.
<r>Thank you in advance for your effort.</r>
Best regards,
Nina Falk

task.en:
Your neighbor had a loud party until late at night over the weekend. You write him an email.

1. Reason for your email
2. What you experienced over the weekend
3. Why this bothers you
4. A suggestion for a compromise

parts.en: Subject: The party over the weekend
Hi Tom,
<r>I wanted to quickly tell you that</r> I want neither to argue nor to be rude, but I need to talk to you about the party over the weekend.
<r>On Saturday</r> you all partied until almost three in the morning, and the music was very loud the whole time.
<r>This means for me that</r> I couldn't sleep all night, and I found that really unpleasant and a bit inconsiderate.
<r>I suggest that</r> we not only talk briefly but also let each other know in advance next time.
<r>I hope you understand what I mean.</r>
Take care,
Alex Berg

task.en:
You reserved a special offer item in a shop last week and wanted to pick it up today. However, you cannot keep the appointment. Write an email to customer service.

1. Reason for your email
2. Why you cannot keep the appointment
3. When you would like to pick up the item instead
4. A request for confirmation

parts.en: Subject: Postponement of my pickup appointment
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you regarding my reservation</r>, which I made last week, because I unfortunately cannot keep the pickup appointment today.
<r>Unfortunately, I cannot keep the appointment</r> because I have to go to a short-notice doctor's appointment today. Before I can come to you, the shop will already be closed.
<r>I would like to</r> come by to pick up the item on Friday afternoon instead, if that's possible for you.
<r>I would be grateful if</r> you could let me know briefly. You don't need to call specially for that — a short email is completely enough.
<r>Thank you for your understanding.</r>
Best regards,
Julia Neumann

task.en:
You had arranged with a friend to go shopping together on Saturday. Now you unfortunately have to cancel. Write him a letter.

1. Reason for your letter
2. Why you have to cancel
3. An apology
4. A suggestion for a new date

parts.en: Berlin, 8 March 2025
Dear Tom,
<r>I unfortunately have to write and tell you that</r> I can't keep our Saturday plan as arranged, because I've completely overbooked myself.
<r>The reason is that</r> I have to work on Saturday after all, even though I was actually supposed to have the day off.
<r>I'm really sorry about that,</r> and I apologize sincerely for it.
<r>How about</r> we meet next weekend instead? Because I would really look forward to that.
<r>See you soon, and sorry again.</r>
Take care,
Mark Fischer

task.en:
You ordered a coffee machine online a week ago. Today the package arrived, but the machine is damaged. Write an email to customer service.

1. Reason for your email
2. What is wrong with the item
3. What you expect instead
4. A request for a quick reaction

parts.en: Subject: Complaint – damaged coffee machine
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I would like to file a complaint</r>, because I did not receive the machine I ordered, but instead a damaged package.
<r>More specifically,</r> the lid is cracked, even though according to your advertising every device is carefully checked before shipping.
<r>I therefore expect</r> that, despite the transport damage, you will send me a replacement quickly, because I urgently need the machine.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> react quickly, because I had specifically chosen this model.
<r>I expect your response within a few days.</r>
Best regards,
Anna Vogel

task.en:
You ordered something online ten days ago, but the delivery still hasn't arrived. Write a letter to customer service.

1. Reason for your letter
2. Details about your order
3. Why the delivery time matters to you
4. A request for information

parts.en: Frankfurt, 20 April 2025
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> I placed an order with you ten days ago, but the delivery has not yet arrived, even though the delivery time has long since expired.
<r>For your information:</r> my order has the number 48213, and I placed it on 10 April.
<r>This matters to me because</r> I urgently need the item. After having waited ten days already, it's really time.
<r>Could you please tell me</r> where my order actually is right now? I would also like to know when I can finally expect it.
<r>I look forward to a quick reply.</r>
Best regards,
David Berger

task.en:
You received a payment reminder for an invoice that you already paid two weeks ago. Write an email to the company.

1. Reason for your email
2. When and how you paid
3. Why the reminder surprised you
4. A request for a review

parts.en: Subject: Payment reminder – already paid
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> I received a payment reminder today for an invoice that I already paid two weeks ago.
<r>For your information:</r> I already paid the amount by bank transfer at the end of the month, and I also have a receipt for it.
<r>I was therefore very surprised,</r> because the payment should have reached you long ago.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> check this: either the payment has not yet been recorded, or there is a mistake.
<r>Thank you for clarifying this quickly.</r>
Best regards,
Nina Falk

task.en:
A friend gave you a tip about a shop with great discounts. You shopped there and saved a lot of money. Write her a letter.

1. Reason for your letter
2. What you bought
3. How much you saved
4. Thanks for the tip

parts.en: Cologne, 5 May 2025
Dear Sabine,
<r>I just had to write and tell you that</r> I went to the shop you recommended, and it was really the best tip from you!
<r>I bought myself</r> the discounted shoes, and they fit me perfectly.
<r>Just imagine,</r> I saved a ton of money doing it, because the shoes were almost fifty percent off.
<r>I therefore want to</r> thank you very much for this tip, because without you I would never have found the shop.
<r>Let's go shopping together again soon!</r>
Take care,
Alex Berg

topic.en: An appointment to open an account

task.en:
You want to open a checking account, but the online form doesn't work. Write an email to the bank and ask for an appointment at the branch.

1. Reason for your email
2. What the problem is
3. When you would have time
4. A request to confirm the appointment

parts.en: Subject: Appointment request for opening an account
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> I would like to open a checking account, but the online form unfortunately doesn't work — it might be due to a technical error.
<r>More specifically,</r> the page gets stuck at the last step, and my data cannot be saved.
<r>I would prefer</r> an appointment this week, because I still have time until I go on holiday.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> let me know briefly by email that the appointment is confirmed. I am already looking forward to the meeting.
<r>Thank you for your effort.</r>
Best regards,
Julia Neumann

task.en:
Your friend works at a bank. You don't understand the account fees and interest on your latest bank statement. Write him a letter.

1. Reason for your letter
2. What exactly you don't understand
3. Why this matters to you
4. A request for a meeting or a call

parts.en: Stuttgart, 14 June 2025
Dear Tobias,
<r>I have a favor to ask you</r>, because due to the complicated account fees I don't understand my latest bank statement.
<r>More specifically,</r> some of the items with the interest are completely unclear to me, and I don't know what they stand for.
<r>This matters to me because</r> I want to have clarity about my money, and you know much more about this than I do.
<r>Could you maybe take some time</r> and call me? You're the only one I would trust with this.
<r>Thanks in advance!</r>
Take care,
Mark Fischer

task.en:
Your bank card was stolen yesterday. You immediately had it blocked by phone. Write an email to your bank.

1. Reason for your email
2. What exactly happened
3. What you have already done
4. A request for a replacement card

parts.en: Subject: Theft of my bank card
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> my bank card was stolen from me yesterday evening.
<r>More specifically,</r> I immediately called the card-blocking hotline, and the card is now blocked.
<r>I have also</r> already informed the police and filed a report, which will hopefully help clarify the case quickly.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> send me a replacement card quickly. I would also like to know whether that is free of charge.
<r>Thank you for your quick help.</r>
Best regards,
Anna Vogel

task.en:
You want to cancel your home contents insurance because you found a cheaper provider. Write a letter to the insurance company.

1. Reason for your letter
2. The date you want to cancel
3. Why you are switching
4. A request for written confirmation

parts.en: Dresden, 2 November 2025
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I hereby cancel my contract</r>, even though I have been satisfied with your insurance coverage so far.
<r>I am cancelling</r> my insurance coverage as of 31 December, that is, at the end of this year.
<r>The reason for this is</r> that I found a cheaper provider within the notice period, and I want to save money by doing so.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> confirm the cancellation in writing. Also, the most important thing for me is that everything is done on time.
<r>Thank you for your understanding.</r>
Best regards,
David Berger

topic.en: Reply to the invitation for a consultation

task.en:
Your insurance company invited you to a free consultation. You want to attend, but suggest a different date. Write an email in reply.

1. Thanks for the invitation
2. Why the proposed date doesn't work
3. Your suggested date
4. A request for confirmation

parts.en: Subject: Reply to your invitation for a consultation
Dear Ms. Weber,
<r>Thank you very much for your invitation</r> to the consultation, and I would love to take part.
<r>Unfortunately, the proposed date doesn't work for me,</r> because I already have a doctor's appointment that day before I could come to you.
<r>Would it be possible</r> to find a different date, next Friday for example? Then I would definitely have time.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> confirm briefly whether the new date is possible. Despite my full schedule, I would gladly make time for it.
<r>I look forward to our conversation.</r>
Best regards,
Nina Falk

task.en:
You cancelled your contract on time, but the company keeps withdrawing money from your account. Write an email to the company.

1. Reason for your email
2. When and how you cancelled
3. What has happened since then
4. A request for an immediate refund

parts.en: Subject: Continued charges despite cancellation
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> you keep withdrawing money from my account, even though I cancelled on time.
<r>For your information:</r> I already cancelled my contract in writing six weeks ago, and I also received a confirmation for it.
<r>Nevertheless,</r> money has still been withdrawn from my account twice since then.
<r>I therefore ask you to</r> refund the missing amounts immediately. I would also like to receive written confirmation of the cancellation.
<r>I expect your reply within one week.</r>
Best regards,
Alex Berg

topic.en: Sick note after eating at a snack stand

task.en:
You ate something from a snack stand yesterday evening and have felt very unwell ever since. You cannot come to work today. Write an email to your boss.

1. Reason for your email
2. What you ate
3. What the doctor said
4. Until when you will probably be absent

parts.en: Subject: Sick note for today
Hi Tom,
<r>I unfortunately have to let you know that</r> I can't come to work today. If I had known how sick I would feel, I wouldn't have touched the food yesterday.
<r>More specifically,</r> I ate a sausage from the snack stand yesterday evening, and I've felt really bad ever since.
<r>The doctor said</r> that it's probably a mild case of food poisoning, and that's why I feel dizzy and weak.
<r>I think</r> I should let my colleague know, because I will probably be absent until Friday.
<r>I'll be in touch as soon as I feel better.</r>
Take care,
Julia Neumann

task.en:
You recently thought about your school days with your friend, when there was often pizza in the cafeteria. You invite him to a cooking evening at your place. Write him a letter.

1. Reason for your letter
2. What you remembered
3. What you would like to cook together
4. When he can come over

parts.en: Bremen, 9 October 2025
Dear Felix,
<r>I recently had to think of you because</r> I was thinking about our school days, when there was always pizza in the cafeteria.
<r>Do you remember</r> how much we loved the taste of that pizza back then? And how we always laughed together?
<r>I would love to</r> recreate that famous pizza from back then with you, because I finally found a good recipe.
<r>Would you be free this weekend?</r> I could cook on Saturday, but you'd need to let me know briefly beforehand so I can shop in time.
<r>I'm already looking forward to our cooking evening!</r>
Take care,
Mark Fischer

task.en:
A friend helped you change your diet half a year ago. Now you have achieved a lot. Write him an email.

1. Reason for your email
2. What has changed for you
3. Why this matters to you
4. Thanks for his help

parts.en: Leipzig, 14 April 2026
Dear Tobias,
<r>I've wanted to write to you for a long time, because</r> I have consciously changed my diet over the last few months. That's why I feel much better now.
<r>More specifically,</r> I have lost five kilos, and I no longer eat as unhealthily as before.
<r>This matters to me because</r> I have become a better version of myself, and that simply feels great.
<r>I therefore want to thank you very much,</r> because your tips were really helpful for my successful journey.
<r>Let's cook together again sometime soon!</r>
Take care,
Anna Vogel

task.en:
You want to bake a cake for your daughter's birthday, but you no longer remember your grandmother's family recipe exactly. Write her a letter.

1. Reason for your letter
2. What occasion you need the cake for
3. What you still remember about the recipe
4. A request for her to send you the recipe

parts.en: Nuremberg, 3 August 2025
Dear Grandma,
<r>I have a favor to ask you</r>, because I would like to use your family recipe for Julia's birthday cake.
<r>I'm planning</r> to bake a cake, and it would be nice if it tasted just like yours.
<r>The problem is</r> that I no longer remember all the ingredients that you used back then, and I don't want to get anything wrong.
<r>Could you</r> maybe write down the recipe and send it to me? That would be a great help to me.
<r>I'm already looking forward to sharing the cake with you.</r>
Lots of love,
David Berger

task.en:
Two weeks ago you took part in a survey about eating habits. You have not yet received the promised results. Write an email to the organizers.

1. Reason for your email
2. When and in what you took part
3. What was promised to you
4. A request for the results

parts.en: Subject: Results of your survey on eating habits
Dear Sir or Madam,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> I have not yet received the promised results of the survey, even though two weeks have already passed since then.
<r>As a reminder:</r> I took part in your survey on eating habits two weeks ago, and I gave my email address at the time.
<r>You had promised me</r> that I would automatically be informed after the evaluation, but so far I haven't heard anything from you.
<r>I would be very happy if</r> you could send me the results of the survey. I would also be interested to see how my answers compare to the majority.
<r>Thank you in advance.</r>
Best regards,
Nina Falk

topic.en: Questions about the new snack rule

task.en:
Your child's school has introduced a new rule: only healthy snacks are allowed during the break. You are not sure exactly what that means. Write a letter to the class teacher.

1. Reason for your letter
2. What you have packed so far
3. What you would still like to know
4. A request for a list of allowed snacks

parts.en: Cologne, 21 January 2026
Dear Ms. Klein,
<r>I am writing to you because</r> I have a question about the new rule on healthy snacks, and I'm no longer sure what I can pack for my son.
<r>So far I have usually</r> given him packaged cookies, but now I'm not sure whether that's still okay.
<r>I would be interested to know</r> whether some sweets are still allowed, because my son doesn't like eating fruit.
<r>I would be grateful if</r> you could send me a list of what exactly counts as a healthy snack. I would also welcome some suggestions.
<r>Thank you for your effort.</r>
Best regards,
Alex Berg

task.en:
You have now been living in Germany for a few months, and a certain rule surprised you a lot at first. You write to a friend back home about it and invite her to visit. Write her an email.

1. Reason for your email
2. What surprised you
3. How you have gotten used to it by now
4. An invitation for her to visit

parts.en: Subject: You won't believe what surprised me here!
Dear Katja,
<r>I absolutely have to tell you that</r> I've been living here in Germany for a few months now, and since then a lot of things have surprised me.
<r>What surprised me most</r> was how super strict the rules on waste separation are here, and how seriously everyone takes it.
<r>By now I have</r> gotten used to the rules, and I even find it practical.
<r>I would like to warmly invite you</r> to visit me. Then you will see it all for yourself.
<r>I'm already really looking forward to your visit.</r>
Lots of love,
Julia Neumann

task.en:
